I am a 23 year old female and was in really good shape before I started this program. Even so, the workouts kicked my butt! Insanity will challenge even those in unbelievable shape.
Overall I am very pleased with my purchase. I love these super high energy workouts and actually look forward to them. I love that they are relatively short (average about 45 mintues, less if you skip the time consuming and unnecessary pre-workout stretch). Shaun T and his crew are very motivating. The music isn't great, but isn't bad either.
My only gripe- the warmups. They are very intense and might be an overload for someone not used to warming up that fast. And the fit test has no warm up so you are putting yourself at risk of injury if you go right into it. When I first started I was getting awful headaches whenever I worked out and my chiropractor said it was because I was overloading my system. So I would do my own pre-warm up warm up for a while until my body adjusted.
A side note- I have actually gained weight since I started. I was pretty thin to begin with and doing such intense workouts really increases your appetite! So if you are trying to lose weight, be conscious of that.

Ok here it goes. If you have bad knees, shoulders, or any other body part then this is not for you. If you are already in shape then this will not get you in more shape. Insanity is just a cardio work out and it is difficult at time but there is nothing in the videos that you can't do on your own. For 30 to 60 minutes you will do mainly a leg, calf, thigh, and butt work out with some push ups and abs in there too. Many times through the videos some of the exercises repeat from previous workouts that you have already completed.
My final statement is: If you belong to a gym or have the motivation to do some physical activity with your life the don't buy this.
If you are one of those people who try a new diet or fad every week to try to lose weight or get in shape then try this out waste your money and start something new the next week.
Great workout, unfortunately two of the discs don't work and when replaced still did not work. Great seller to deal with, tried to make it right.
Best workout of my life! It is a great system and will get you into shape fast!

summary: AMAZING!! Even for a beginner like myself!
text: Ok so I purchased Insanity in the beginning of the year, and I tried it once, doing only the fit test and I about died, so needless to say I buried it in my closet until I was ready, I also own p90x and honestly that is so boring I couldn't get past week one, but this is soo much fun great energy. So I am on day 4, and let me just say this is very addictive, and super awesome. I love it, I'm not super fit, well I'm not any kind of fit actually, but I decided after reading review after review, mostly discouraging,to say what the heck I'm going to give it 100% and do this and get an amazing body. I for sure recommend this to anyone! With the right motivation, and discipline you can dig deep and get through it, and it may be hard at first but I know if I can do it I think anybody can. It is totally worth it =)

I ordered the product for my daughter but tried it for myself as well.  I'm in early fifties and fairly fit, but found it was too much for me--the jumping was bothering my knees. (but I had mild knee discomfort before I tried it). My daughter, however, loves it! She has stuck to the time table and has finished her first month and notices a difference in her body and stamina already.  It's a vigorous workout--to keep up you need to be in good physical shape to begin with or just do as much as you can and work up to keeping up.  Shawn T is a great motivator.  Since I ordered the product for my daughter, I'm giving it her rating of 5 stars.
I am 5 weeks into this.  It is pretty pricey, but I have seen results.  I think it is worth it.  He does a long warm-up before stretching.  This is great for preventing soreness and injury.

"Insanity" is the perfect name for this DVD program. Why? Because you have to be at least a little bit insane to jump into a program such as this one. The program is split up into two months of intense cardio and plyometrics with a bit of strength training thrown in (you use your body, not weights). There is also a recovery week in which you'll find yourself doing a lot of stretching, a couple of yoga moves, and plenty of balancing moves. Each DVD includes at least one workout on it (a couple feature two). One DVD focuses strictly on the abs, although the abs get a great workout no matter which DVD you are on. Also included is a workout calendar that lists which DVD to do on each day of the week. Sundays are reserved for resting. The DVD set I purchased also came with a recipe book and a meal plan. All of these items were simple to use.

The first month is very intense, with each workout ranging from thirty five to forty five minutes on average. The second month is brutal, pure and simple. The workout length extends to fifty five minutes on some of the DVDs during the second month.

If you are not used to working out, or even if you consider yourself to be in decent shape, the warm-ups will kill you right away. Do not be discouraged by this. If you stick to it, you will improve. Just three days into the program, I found myself lasting longer and longer before having to sit out or take a brief break. After just a couple of days, I noticed that my arms were already beginning to show signs of tone. My legs looked even better. After two weeks, I started losing inches around my waist.

Every two weeks, you have to take a fit test. My first one was terrible, but the second fit test showed me doubling my performance on all but one (globe jumps) of the tests. Each time after that, my results kept improving. Granted, I didn't double anything afterthat, but you'd be surprised how tough it is to add just two or three more reps of a particular move.

The second month really kicked my body into overdrive. I was doing moves that I would never have dreamed of doing just a few weeks before. The intensity level of the second month is off the charts. Do not be ashamed to stop and take a breather while exercising, you'll need it!

Shaun T is a very positive influence throughout the DVDs. He'll go over each move before asking you to do it and highlights people doing each move properly and/or improperly so that you can learn proper form. If someone's leg needs to be straightened out on the DVD, Shaun helps them achieve correct form. This helps you at home maintain proper form as well.

It is not unusual to see members of the workout group on the DVD simply step out of certain exercises from fatigue. Shaun motivates them (and you) to return back to the workout as soon as safely possible.

What it ultimately boils down to is how much you put into the program. If you're serious about getting in shape, losing weight, or building endurance, you can definitely achieve all of these with "Insanity." I personally lost sixteen total pounds and dropped to the tow holes on my belt. My pants fit looser as do my shirts. I feel a lot better than I've ever felt in a long time. Not to brag, but my arms and shoulders are cut now and my legs actually gained a lot of muscle. My abs feel tight as well, but I still have a little fat to get rid of before I can see that six pack I'm working on. Even with the fat that is remaining on my belly, I can already see a bit of definition in my abdominable area.

After a very short break, I plan on starting the program all over again. Stick with it, and you can become just as insane as the rest of us! Highly recommended.

It's a really good DVD and fairly well put together. My biggest problem with it though is that the stretching is inadequate ESPECIALLY because of all the plyometrics that are done. Jumping around so much can hurt your spine and puts pressure on your joints, they should definitely focus more on stretching, relaxing and lengthening your back during the stretchs to prevent injury. There are a few other points I don't agree with (all within the stretching) so I normally do my own stretching during the allotted time since I know my body and I do other strength training congruently with Insanity. I normally get bored with set workouts, with Insanity it's more of a "I so can't do this today" rather than a "I don't want to because it's boring" so that's good, I just remind myself: "I promise I will do my best. My best will vary from day to day, from hour to hour, from minute to minute but in that minute I will do the very best that I can." (First rule of 10 Golden Rules of CrossFit). Insanity (or any other program) is worth it if you stay with it--always do your very best. 3...2...1...GO!

As has been previously stated, this isn't like any other workout DVD.

Shaun T is motivating enough to make me want to move faster when I barely can. But as hard as this workout is, it's hard for me to convince myself to do it at times. I've been in shape all my life and never been overweight. You should be in shape to begin this program. Getting correct form would be very difficult otherwise. These workouts are also very high impact. Keep it in mind if you live upstairs and the neighbors get annoyed by someone jumping around so hard the walls shake (sorry neighbors). I've done the Turbo Jam and Slim Series workouts from Beach Body as well as this one.

Most of the workouts go something like this: A warm up for about 10 minutes; includes variations of running in place, jumping jacks, etc. This is followed by a period of yoga stretches for another 10 minutes or so. With the exception of Pure Cardio (which is nonstop cardio action), most of the exercises you do in sets of 3, 3 times. Then he gives you a 30 second break (I like to call it a 2 minute break). There is also a 'no crunches' ab dvd, which is also included on the "pure Cardio" dvd... a bit weird of them to act like they're giving you these 3 separate dvds, when due to the repetition of content you're really getting 1. Also there is a 25 minute "fit test"...in which you do some of the Insanity exercises as fast as you can and track how many you could complete in the time alloted, so you can view your progress over time.
The starter workouts are usually about 45 minutes long... which means the actual workout time is only about 20 minutes (with the warm-up, stretching, and cool down comprising the other 25 minutes). In the advanced level, workouts are about 60 minutes long...which means you workout for about 40 minutes. That's a huge jump forward... the workouts virtually double in length even though there is only 15 minutes difference in overall time.
It's hard to get bored while doing these workouts. Boredom is something I feel when I'm uh....not about to die because I can't catch my breath and my muscles are screaming....yeah.
Included also is a calendar that has the recommended order for doing the workouts.
You don't use weights with these workouts, making them very practical for travel. You probably won't build bulky muscles, either...as high reps and no weights lead to a more toned physique and improves endurance. Don't be surprised if you can run a marathon after doing this for 60 days....or at least a 10k!
There is also a nutrition guide, which has some good ideas and tasty recipes. I don't have the money to eat the required 5 times a day though, or the time and tools to prepare meals like that consistently. I imagine if you followed it your results would mirror the "before" and "after" pics, since the diets for workouts like this are designed to work alongside the exercise.

If you have a higher than normal heart rate for any reason, like from drinking too much coffee or taking stimulants... use caution and wear a heart rate monitor. If you feel chest pain, stop!!I'm 27 and got my heart rate up to 228 once because I wasn't watching my heart rate. My heart felt as though it would burst and I threw up all over the floor. I hope that wasn't an over-share... but overdoing it could really hurt if you're not careful.

All in all, these DVDs are worth it if you decide beforehand that you will use them. With the bulky, book-like packaging this set doesn't make a very attractive bookend. I have no doubt it will benefit you and that your heart and body will both be in much better shape after you do these workouts daily for awhile.

I really wanted something that was high cardio and this is it.  It's challenging, but not impossible and I can really see a difference in the inches that have melted off my body in just the first two weeks. I would recommend this to anyone that doesn't mind taking their time to get stronger and getting comfortable with the energy it takes to do the routine. The nutrition plan is great too in that you can choose your menu for the week and it's normal food, you know, nothing with super special ingredients that you have to spend a fortune on.
If your determined and if you can push yourself to do this, then you will see results without a doubt. I'm past my first month and I'm loving it! I feel great after each work-out!

Received the product in 10 days.  Product looks good but defective.  More than half of the DVDs do not work in the DVD player or computer.  Seller stated that he would replace but after more than 2 weeks had not replaced the defective product.  Will return half of emails about defective product.  Would not recommend.  Looking at a product I paid for that does not work.  Purchase at your own risk.

summary: Does what it says, so far.
text:
This product is as advertised. I am entering week 3 and would like to share some observations about the program. First, it is not, by any means, an easy workout. It is 40 min that will test your will to succeed. In the first week my heart rate neared 190BPM, and burned a minimum of 800 calories, sometimes breaking 1100. Just for reference, I am 6'2" about 250 and in fairly good shape. Just before starting the program I was doing a 40 min weight session, and 30 - 40 min of running five days a week. Secondly, it can be a bit rough on the joints. There is a significant amount of high impact, so if you have had joint issues, be sure to wear your brace. Finally, it works. It works very well. In the first 2 weeks I have cut about 9 pounds, 3.5% body fat, and gained 2% muscle. It is amazing to me how well it works.

In short, if you really want to lean up, are very determined, and have 45min a day to spare, this is the best option I have found.I will follow up at the end of the program, and see if the results continue.

This workout will straight up kick ur butt!  I'm on week three, and my cardio fitness has exploded.  Shaun T is motivating and no where near as annoying as most fitness program hosts.  Just one warning, this is not a program for beginners.  You have to be in some form of fitness prior to starting.  I would suggest this program to anyone that works out regularly and wants that at home program that will get you shredded

This is not your typical workout.  It really is the most difficult workout I have ever done.  I am in my last two weeks of insanity, and am literally in the best shape of my life!  The hardest part of the workout is sticking with it.  If you commit, you WILL be in the best shape of your life.  Please note that it is tough on your body, especially your knees, so I highly recommend wearing knee braces from the start, even if you don't have knee problems.  Since I started insanity I have lost inches and have toned all over.  It really is Insane!

The exercises are intense. It's all that jumping around that really makes you feel the burn. It's not a special routine or anything, and your results depend on how hard you push yourself. You get what you work for.
If you are in really poor shape, this is NOT the workout for you. I have a history of knee issues, my joint slips out. But I still do intense exercises and just rest for a few days if it starts to flare up (my top orthopedic surgeon from Hopkins recommended it). I've been able to strengthen the joint that way. The first day I did this workout, I felt a pain in my knee. I stopped for a few minutes, then SLOWLY resumed. I realized that as long as I maintained PROPER FORM my knee was fine. It's easy to get wrapped up in trying to keep up with the group. But Shaun says several times in the video "do not sacrifice proper form" for speed. It helps to work out in front a mirror. I'm not saying anyone else with bad joints should try. Please don't! Save your joints for old age. If you do decide to try it, consult your physician. And remember.. keep proper form!!
I started the program less than 2 weeks ago, so I can't give any final results. I am combining this with a diet packed with fruits and vegetables. I have noticed that my clothes are starting to loosen up. I feel stronger, and have more energy. It will definitely whip you into shape.

This workout is beyond INSANE. The rest periods are short and the work periods are long. It really is great cardio, but I would not recommend going 100% effort on these work bouts. Being degreed in Exercise Science and Certified Performance Coach you have to understand a little science behind this training theory. Going 100% will help you gain more power output than fat loss. 75% effort should be your goal if you want more fat loss. If you are a cardio junky then go for it...balls to the wall! Overall, this video has great bodyweight circuits that you should just try to work on technique on your own. I don't recommend this video for anyone extremely over weight (needing to lose 50+ lbs) or with hip and knee issues. My favorite video is the upper body weight training. Awesome!
Two of the discs in this package do not work and it was advertised as "new" and the user said they had never used it. I wish people would not sell items that do not work.

summary: Very hard, but well worth the effort
text:
Okay, I admit it: my main reason for buying this was that I wanted to lose that extra fat around my mid section (and in some other areas, too).
And guess what? I did lose quite a lot of it! A great side effect is of course that your fitness level increases dramatically!
Make no mistake, in order for this to happen you really have to work out HARD. The workouts themselves are really advanced and I would not recommend them to someone who isn't at least moderately fit. Now, I thought that I was pretty fit when I started out but I still found it really hard to keep up, especially during the first two weeks. Some of the exercises I had to do more slowly; others, like the power push-ups in the Max workouts I still can do only three or so and then I have to do regular push-ups because I just don't have enough strength.
However, tomorrow is my last Max Insanity workout day and I think I will start over again and the next time around I might just conquer those power push-ups, too!
The nutrition guide is of course very helpful, however, I was already eating healthy foods to begin with and I already follow most of those guidelines anyway. They are totally right, however, when they say you must eat healthy and wholesome foods if you want to be able to get the full effects of these workouts. You can't do them by eating junk food.

In my opinion Insanity is great for people who are willing to work out hard and who want to improve their general fitness level. I know I will keep doing Insanity in months (and hopefully years) to come, no longer six days a week, but 2-3 times per week and mixed up with my running and other workouts at the gym.

I bought this program and Shawn T is amazing, it is a real challenge, and harder than PX90 in my opinion.

Word of caution...this is a true challenege, if you have knee problems, skip this, it isn't for you...

I have been using these DVDs for 2 weeks now, and although the calendar claims you should work out 6 days out of 7, I find that hard. The first week my calves hurt so hard that I could barely walk. People were stopping me at work, and giving me their condolences because they recognized the "insanity" walk! (note that the people who noticed this were all in killer shape).

The videos are the most intense I've ever used, and I've stopped going to the gym at all since buying this program. It is much easier to drag myself out of bed at 4am and turn on the TV than it is to get dressed and drive to the gym, so I am more inclined to work out when there's less effort involved in getting there. This is fortunate, since you will need every stitch of extra effort just to complete the exercises. However, at least the first half of the program is short, and once the warmup is done (yes, you will be dripping sweat just from that), and the stretch is done, there's really only 15-20 minutes of really intense exercise to endure.

Like others have said, you should be in decent shape when you start this program. There is a lot of jumping, a lot of push-ups, and you bend a whole lot to touch the ground at breakneck speed. Shaun T is extremely influential, and the wide array of tight abs and buns on display by the workout crew is inspiring enough to keep me going. The fact that Shaun T's workout crew also has to stop for breaks, just like I do, makes me feel less like a lazy, slovenly alien than I did with other, over-produced videos.

Make sure you wear a heart-rate monitor every time, and pay attention to it. Your body will tell you when you should just be jogging in place for a minute, and when to get back in the race with the crew.

Because I am building so much muscle, I have not lost a single pound yet, but I have lost about 3 inches off my hips and an inch off of my waist. As a horse owner, my horseback riding--which depends on core and thigh strength--has improved tenfold, so I know that it's working. I actually look forward to working out now, because the results are worth the quick spurt of energy I expend every morning.
My wife and I are only through the 1st month, and the program is wearing us out!  I guess I'll deduct a couple of stars if they kill me in month 2.

summary: Great product. Fun and challenging. Perfect for the passionate and motivated.
text: This is such a great workout. It's fun, challenging, and gives your body great results. I greatly recommend to anyone.

Insanity is an intense in-home workout series developed by Shaun T.  I've been on it for a month and can see/feel a big difference.  The main reason I got it was because I travel a lot with my job and it's hard to keep a solid work out routine with different gym hours and equipment in different places.  Carrying the DVDs and a DVD player with me allows me to keep up consistent work outs anywhere I go.  You do not need much space or any specialized equipment (e.g. pull up bars, weights, etc.).  It is hard at first ... even the warm ups kicked my butt, but if you stay with it you will continue to improve.  It is hard on the joints (knees and shoulders) especially if you don't keep your form correct on several of the moves, so don't try this if you have problems with either.  Ultimately, it is an intense, effective work out that goes where you go ... definitely worth the investment!

summary: this is hardcore and worth every minute!
text: not that i own every cardio dvd out there, but i do have a good collection.  by far, this is the most challenging workout dvd i own.  if you're serious about getting into shape, this is it. there is no 'filler-moves/minutes' in this dvd collection. every minute of the workout will kick your butt into shape.  NOW, DON'T BE INTIMIDATED BY ALL THE REVIEWS OF THIS BEING THE HARDEST WORKOUT EVER ON DVD.  yes, it is hard, but as long as you're in some sort of decent shape, you'll get through it and eventually become stronger each week (even the people in the dvds are taking breaks through out the workout).  if you can get through billy blank's ultimate-boot-camp, you can do 'insanity,' although this is much harder.  the first 10 minutes of the workout is the hardest, but once you get through that, you'll be able to finish the workout.  as for the instructor, shaun-t, he is great.  he is experienced and actually does a great job motivating you without being annoying.  as for the background music, (you have option to turn-off the music) it is actually motivating, not some annoying-wanna-be-club/dance music.  as for results, i started seeing myself literally shrink by the end of week 2.  not only did the pounds come off, but i saw how toned my body was getting each week.  my arms and abs now have definition (went through 3 pregnancies with 60 lb weigh gain each time).  i finished the 2 month program, and i still use the dvds (2-3 times a week) mixed in with my rotation of 'physique 57,' 'billy-blank's ultimate bootcamp,' and 'piloxing.'  so, get this if you're serious about getting into shape.....HAPPY 'INSANITY!!!'

This workout is pushing me to the limits.  I am now 2 weeks into it and am starting to see core muscles that I didn't know I had.  That being said, I'm a 48 year old woman and, if I didn't already workout regularly, I wouldn't be able to do "Insanity."  Right now, I'm only getting through about 60-70% of the entire main workout without taking extra water breaks.  The workout takes your heart rate to the 85% limit for long stretches of time.  Don't try this workout without being in reasonable decent physical condition first.  This is not a "I wanna lose weight and haven't worked out in a while..." type workout.  I'm using it to get over a plateau that a reached while running and lifting weights.  Hopefully, I'll be able to finish the whole 60 days.  The only reason I'm rating it a 4 instead of a 5 is that I can't rate the whole workout yet.

This is an awesome workout!  I would say it's a little more than insane to begin with, but once you get rolling, it's really a rush to see how you can transform yourself and really pretty much just whip yourself into shape in a short period of time.

This product is amazing. I am literally drenched in sweat within the first 5 minutes, and you can definitely feel the results the next day. I've tried out a lot of different workout videos ranging from Jillian Micheals to Crunch yoga, and I can definitely say that this one is my favorite. It's not easy, but it's definitely worth it.

Workout is great when the dvd will play.  Tried several of the  dvd's in three different players and they will not play smoothly in any of them.  Emailed the seller about exchange for new dvd's and get no return email back

summary: The savior for this post-partum body
text:
As a former gym employee and overall well-educated person in terms of fitness and nutrition, I always thought that once I gave birth, I would bounce right back. WRONG!!! I tried everything I used to do, which used to work, but the truth of the matter is that this body needed a SHOCK, and boy did Shaun T. deliver that.

As I mentioned, I was a "normal" weight person when I got pregnant, not at the best I could be, but not at the worst, but when I stopped losing weight after those first two post-partum months, I started to get really frustrated, depressed, and discouraged. I was in a rut. I hated the gym, and I started seeing watching my food intake as a waste of time. But I heard from a few co-workers about Insanity and gave it a shot.

If I could personally hug and thank Shaun T, I would. It's difficult, and I will say that you should already be used to some kind of exercise before starting; otherwise, it might prove too difficult and discourage you further, but if you have been hitting the gym and pounding the treadmill and all that and see nothing changing, this is the program for you. It will shock your body and your metabolism and your muscles, show you that you are capable of more than you thought, and overall, keep you from abusing your body with junk. After all, when you work THAT hard, you don't want to undo what you've done. This is a great program for the body, but also for the mind. Cravings, gone. Hopelessness over body, gone. Bad mood, gone. I am still not where I want to be, but the results have been dramatic nevertheless.

Again, I wouldn't recommend this for beginners to exercise and fitness or for anyone who is very overweight or has joint problems. But, this is a lifesaver for those of you stuck in quicksand fighting to get results and seeing none and wasting your precious time pounding your head against the wall because you see no changes.

P.S. The nutrition plan is easy to follow, not expensive, and very satisfying. I have a big appetite, and I was never hungry or grossed out; nor was it one of those plans that costs you hundreds every week in ingredients that are eccentric or hard to find and that you will use once and throw away when it spoils.

I love Insanity. :-)

summary: Being insane means to be able to change life
text:
First at all I like to say that I bought this DVD collection as an Import because I live in Germany and this product is not meant for the german market so far. I`ve read that some people have problems with playing the discs. So far I can say that I do not have these problems.
I`ve done Billy Blanks before and thought I can easily switch to Insanity - deffinetly not.
Insanity is a 60 day workout that is linked to maximum fitness results. I`m in week four now and have to say that this is really intense. Four weeks ago when I started this workout I knew that it would be intense, but I never thought that it would be such an incredible sweaty affair.
In month 1 you do workouts with a running time of 40 minutes. Actually these workouts are about 25 minutes, because you do stretching and have water breaks of 30 seconds. It is hard to believe that you can get in shape in 25 minutes, right? I can tell you that I burned 557kcal in 25 minutes. Shaun T says you can burn up to 1000kcal. I think this is deffinetly possible, especially when we think of the workouts in month two which have a running time of an hour. I`ve done the Pure cardio workout + Cardio abs today (week 4 day 1) and I burned 673kcal.
Talking about a diet: You can not take a diet! Please, don`t do this to your body. Your body needs a normal healthy nutrition to refuel energy. If you want to do a diet then you shouldn`t do Insanity. The right formula is to change nutrition. Eat right - feel right. The nutrition plan is a great opportunity to get some ideas of how to do that. In my opinion you do not need protein shakes! Instead of protein shakes I eat tuna and cottage cheese. Eat some eggs (not too many) and combine it with a fresh salad. Salads are always welcome.
Especially tuna has a huge amount of proteins! Furthermore I recommend oatmeal in the morning in combination with peach and milk. Eat some veggies and fruits among your meals. According to the Insanity nurtrition plan you should eat five meals a day. Sounds very complicated but it`s deffintely manageable.
So far (week 4 day 1) I lost about 10,4 lbs. I`m very happy about it but have to say that this workout is deffintely not for everybody. If you have knee issues you shouldn`t do this workout because you do a lot of jumps and a lot of other knee work. You will feel the change immediately but you will see the results at about week two. Your body needs to prepare for the great change so don`t be disappointed if you don`t see the "great changes" in three days. Your muscles will change too! You don`t need extra weights for this workout because you do a lot of push ups and you work your arms all the time.
You will feel very tired - that is absolutely normal! Please make sure to sleep enough because your body needs this rest to recover and to build muscles, furthermore you burn fat while you sleep.
Last thing: Please stay motivated! As I said before this workout is really intense, especially the first week is a hard drill. This is normal because your body gets confronted with unknown moves. You will always sweat like ;-)
As long as you focus on your mind and your will it`s gonna be okay. One important thing at all: Go at your own speed at your own pace. You are always allowed to take a break - do it.
Insanity is awesome!

The product was shipped quick and good condition.  I have had just one of the dvds that skipped during one of the videos.  I did not get with the seller as i was not worried about it so not his fault.  otherwise very pleased with the product and service.

Recieved product in a timely manner, but some of the videos are messed up. some skip around like they were burned and some are scratchy. very disappointed!!!! Trying to save money didn't payoff for me....

summary: Great Workout...A couple of minor irritations-
text:
My fiance and I are 3 weeks in and have already seen substantial gains in our fit test scores. I have lost about an inch off of my waist, but my fiance's progress has been a bit slower as of this review after doing the same workout each night and eating essentially the same diet. I think that she will catch up by the end of the program though.

The workouts themselves are intense and will challenge you to your breaking point and then some...but you get strong-and I mean crazy strong, really quickly...especially your core. That being said, I find elements of the workouts to be just a bit repetitive at times, especially the stretching and warmup routines that are VERY similar on each dvd for the first 4 weeks of the program. I would have enjoyed some variety in these from workout to workout to stretch my muscles in some different ways.

The other thing that bugs me a little bit is that while Shaun T is challenging me to "dig deeper" and "push" during the DVDs, he often stops performing the exercises when things get particularly intense to go "critique" one of the other performer's form. I realize that speaking while doing a workout is intense, but when I am struggling and feel my thighs on fire, it irritates me when he stops working out and starts walking around the room...It typically results in my yelling some unfriendly words to my onscreen fitness trainer during my workout. Overall, this program has been great for us and I look forward to moving to P90x when we're done with this to build on the base we're making here.

I actually purchased Insanity about 3 months ago but I am just now getting to leaving a review. A little about me. 36 years old, 6'2" 215lbs. Lifetime athlete and I remained very fit until I had knee surgery in 2003. Followed with getting married and following that up with kids. Needless to say I began to put on weight after knee surgery in '03 because I was no longer playing ball and not being as active. In January of 2009 I topped out at 240lbs and just became totally sick of myself. I started eating better and started back running and lifting weights and got myself back into shape (down to 210lbs). By January of 2010 I became bored with the lifting and running routine and needed something new. I had eased back up to 222lbs but was still pretty fit. I saw the Insanity infomercials and was very intrigued. It reminded me of the hardcore plyometric exercises from high school athletics that made me want to vomit but also got me into shape real quick. I brought Insanity and here is what I think:

1) You have to be in shape to start this program! Period. A couch potato could not properly complete this program. It is very physically demanding and will push you to the limit. After the first two days I could not even bend over to tie my shoes. My legs felt as if Eddie and Charlie Murphy had beat them up because I ground my muddy shoes into Eddie's couch. You will be completely sore! The month one interval workout literally made my heart hurt the first time I did it. My heart was sore after that workout like a muscle would be. I dont have a monitor but it must have been near max on the BPM for most of the workout. I was totally wiped out early on by the workouts and I came in in pretty good shape. Your body does eventually adjust to the intensity but the workouts NEVER get easy. You suck wind and fall over on day one and you suck wind and fall over on day 60.

2) You have to know your body! One of my knees has been cut and the other probably could use some cleanup. Years of basketball have taken a toll on them. But guess what? I finished the program and have begun round two of Insanity. During the Recovery week I injured my lower back doing a supplemental weight lifting workout. It hindered my Insanity workouts for about 3 weeks. In fact I had to finally take a week off to heal up. But once I came back, it was all good! If you know your body, and I guess have no MAJOR impediments, you CAN do this workout. I know to start out kind of slow after the warm up is over and let my body have about 3 minutes to get acclimated to the intense movements. I know that if my knees are having a bad day dont dip all the way down on the squats or try for maximum air on the jumps. Its that easy. Work around any limitations your body may have.

3) You will get addicted if you take it seriously. Results come so fast with Insanity that you get addicted to it. By "results" I dont necessarily mean that dramatic weight loss is guaranteed. I really only "lost" 7lbs during the program. I mean your body changes QUICK!!!! Your stamina and strength gains are very noticeable just 2 weeks in. By a month in I felt 10 years younger and indestructable. And although I only lost 7lbs I look very different. People constantly tell me how much younger and skinnier I look. The weight you lose in Insanity is that "good" weight. Pure fat. My body has gotten so much more tapered because I know fat has been lost and muscle has been gained. So even though the workouts can be miserable, and often leave me balled over on the floor with sweat pouring off me and snot hanging off my nose, I cant get enough of them. Each time I do one I feel a little better. A little stronger.

And let me say I am not even very strict with my diet. I pretty much eat reasonably but I in no way follow the diet plan. The fact that I can be so pleased with the results of a workout plan but have not really changed my lifestyle is phenomenal. I eat how I ate before. I actually spend less time working out than I did before. A trip to the gym use to be about 2hours and occured 4-5 days a week for me. Insanity is an hour and is 5-6 days a week for me. The Insanity workout is so efficient that you dont need to be in the gym two hours. In fact, the 59 minute Interval and 55 minute Plyo workouts in month two are pretty much the limit of "normal" non-Olympic athlete capabilities for a human in my opinion. Anything longer and a heart attack would be almost certain.

Some people have complained about the length of the warm-up and stretching sessions in the workouts but I think they are totally necessary. For me, there is no way my knees and back could take that pounding without proper priming. I think Insanity is a lifetime type fitness program and not something faddish. If you are or were an athlete you have to appreciate the purity and simplicity of the movements in this program. You can tailor the workout routine to fit around weight lifting, running or athletic events. I have incorporated upper body weight lifting a couple of days a week recently because I will admit the program mostly focuses on legs, chest and shoulders. Pull ups, curls, dips and other upper body weight workouts are good supplements. One other note: The Cardio Abs routine is great! However, a friend let me borrow the Ab Ripper X DVD from P90X and I find that ab routine a little more challenging. There is a greater diversity of movements in the Ab Ripper routine and no down time. You get about 3 breaks in the Insanity ab routine. Both the Insanity and P90X ab DVD's are a little over 16 minutes and very effective. I would give the Insanity version 4.5 stars to P90X's 5 stars. But I absolutely LOVE this Insanity program and will continue it in some form or fashion as long as my body allows!

text:
Open the asylum. Shaun T's Insanity from Beachbody provides one of the most grueling cardio programs available. Shaun T. enjoys great popularity with his body shaping dance videos. Insanity is something altogether different. Hear me, this is not a weight loss program and it is NOT designed for the sedentary. Insanity's 60 day program builds endurance and strength for the serious athlete or the exercise enthusiast.

The good news is once you buy the DVDs you do not need to purchase anything more to successfully complete the routines. A nutrition guide comes with program. I highly recommend you follow it to achieve maximum results. Other suggestions include: wear a good pair of cross trainer shoes, use an exercise mat and work out in a place where you can sweat profusely, as you will perspire like rain during the daily exercises.

I've been reading reviews of the Insanity program from various sources. It's clear to me that like many things in life, you get what you put into it. I took a lot away from the 60 day challenge. I found this to be as mentally and physically challenging as anything I've ever encountered. Physically, I am now at a personal peak. Furthermore, I improved on my Fit Test at each two week interval and made significant gains from beginning to end.

It wasn't a joy ride, though. I sustained minor injuries to my toe, hand, and wrist, as well as irritating my right knee. So many times I wanted to stop, not just the program overall, but actually stop mid-exercise. I wanted to throw up my hands and scream, "Why am I torturing myself?" Honestly, I can't tell you how I found the will in those moments to "dig deeper," but somehow I did. However, I can unequivocally tell you I am thrilled I did. Now, not only do I feel good, but I know there is something inside of me that can go further and push harder.

No, I was not in awesome or even great shape when I started this, like most people who seem into this workout. And I should mention I am only on Week 3, but the results are AMAZING, already.
What I love about INSANITY is that I really feel like I have accomplished something at the end of each workout. I see the results in my body (I take a photo of myself at the beginning of each week as a reminder).
The important things to know are: 1) it's okay to modify the exercise (assuming you are familiar with the techniques) if you don't quite have the physical strength yet, 2) knowing some good breathing techniques will help you immensely, because this will really push you to the limit, 3) Go at your own pace, because whatever it is, it will still give you results, 4)you absolutely must be good to your body...no hard landings.
I see the most dramatic change so far in my core. Everything is stronger, tighter. I think you need to be able to do a boot camp style workout in order to be able to do this successfully. I took one at my local gym before starting this and I am really glad I did because this is way more intense.
In addition to the physical changes, I have to say there is an emotional boost to doing this. I feel awesome about how much I have improved already, and just how I am doing something that makes me really sweat.
My only, paltry gripe is that I wish the meal plan had some on the go style options, because I am a grad student and I have to eat on the go a lot.

text:
Hi All,

I'm an independent Beachbody Coach, INSANITY enthusiast, and 13 days away from my P90X graduation.

INSANITY is a great program, not for the light at heart. They repeatedly warn people of the possible stresses and injuries that may be incurred while participating in this fitness program. With that said, it is probably the best weight/fat loss program put to DVD.

The moves are varied, but simple enough that you can replicate them. The training consists of jumps, squats, running in place, plank, low-plank, and C-sit positions. I really like the emphasis on the core and the lower back and abdominal strength you will acquire over the 60 days.

Don't worry about not being able to finish a certain routine. Even Shaun T has to take breaks! Just try your best and you will see great results. There is no equipment necessary other than a heartrate monitor. The workouts range from 39 minutes to 58 minutes depending on the DVD and phase you are in.

I like this meal plan because it is simple, easy to follow, and gives suggestions for in between meal snacks. You will be consuming a lot of calories, but it is assumed that you burn over 600 per session of INSANITY.

You want lean 6-pack action with little startup investment, then this program is for you!

I have written a nice comparison to P90X on my blog if you are interested in reading more about them.[...]

If you need help, encouragement, convincing, or a coach, feel free to contact me via [...]

Dig Deeper!

Andy

I am not really overweight, but not in great shape either. The problem I have with these videos is 1) The warmup is 20 minutes long and will wear you out before you can do the actual workout.
2) There is no upper body included in the warmups so when you are spent, you've only done legs and cardio.
3) Even if I could do the full 40 minutes, I do not look forward to taking that much time from my day to get a workout.

There are better programs that can whip you into shape in less time. If you are finishing these workouts, you are already in good shape. As others have mentioned, people in the class on the video are dropping out during the warmup phase.

On a positive note, the production value is outstanding. Shaun T is motivational, and not annoying to listen to. The music is not your typical electronic repetitive rhythm, but it's more of an orchestral Rocky-type soundtrack, which is great.

However, if you are looking to do a workout that only takes about 20 minutes and will really work your muscles and cardio, I recommend: Jillian Michaels - 30 Day Shred The production value is much lower, and I have to turn the volume down so I don't have to listen to her, but I just play my own music on the stereo.

I thought I was in decent shape, but insanity kicked my tail. I've seen a huge improvement so far and I am three weeks in. Shaun T is an excellent fitness instructor and keeps you motivated the entire time. If you are looking to change up your routine and have a challenge, I recommend Insanity. Just remember, do not give up so quick because it gets easier as the days go by and you will start to see results. My husband and I have. The best part is we can do it all at home without the expense of a gym, weights or equipment.

If you are in ok shape or just starting out, DO NOT get this program. I was a 5 day a week powerlifter while also mixing in jogging and cycling for cardio. I thought I was in really good shape. Then I got Insanity and everything was turned upside down.

This program is intense...no other way to state it. I heard that it was intense before I got it, but you can't understand until you experience it. I will say again...this program is INTENSE. After about two days into the program I could feel my body reacting. They say this may be the hardest workout ever put on dvd, and I agree. I now do P90X on my days off from insanity because it doesn't even feel like a workout anymore. For the first week even trying to sit down to use the bathroom was painful because my legs were so obliterated.

I see all these infomercials about ab rockers, total fitness (sorry Chuck Norris)machines, shake weights (really??? stand there and shake a weight?? no thanks)...and all these claims that you can get miraculous results with minimal time and effort. Well if you buy into that notion you should not get insanity. With this program you need about an hour a day and MAXIMUM effort. Your body (and your significant other...when they look at your body..) will thank you.

The only negative I can say about this program is that for some of the exercises you need a fairly high ceiling, especially if you are a taller person. There are a lot of jumping exercises with your arm extended upwards. My ceiling isnt high enough for that...but it's an easy adjustment, just don't reach up as high. This program is worth the price ten fold.

If you have knee or shoulder problems this is not for you.

I am 55 years old and have done Beachbody's P90X about three times and P90X plus about three times.  Like many fans of their DVDs I was psyched to try this one as well.  The first week I tried Insanity I think I threw up twice.  P90X Plyometrics is a day off compared to this workout series.  After my 60 days were up I felt like I could climb Everest.  This is pure, flat out cardio and plyometric floor work with no weights and few breaks.  Make no mistake about it, this is one tough workout.  If you are looking for a good next step after P90X or a cardio program to interleave with your weight training and are in pretty good shape I highly recommend this one.  Although you will be taking plenty of breaks the first few weeks, I noticed that after doing it for several months as part of my weight rotation, I could make it all the way through without a break.  I bought this program for my sister and my girlfriend because they were afraid that weight training would cause them to bulk up and they swear by it.  If you are into lifting you will find you will lose some muscle mass in the 60 day program and may, if you continue with it, want to work it into some kind of weight training.  There is a 13 disk expanded version that includes an upper body weight training DVD that is pretty great as well.  Shaun T is a very good trainer and will yell at you as opposed to Tony Horton who cuts you more slack.  The cast is good as well and there is no hiding the fact that the workouts are kicking their butts.  Get through this workout series and you will have major bragging rights.

summary: You CAN do this even if you're not in great shape
text:
I cannot say enough good things about this wonderful workout!!! After just a few workouts, I already feel stronger in my core and I feel my body changing rapidly.

I am recovering from a long bout of illness and started exercising about 3 months ago. I'm 45 pounds overweight and I'm not in amazing shape. It is really safe. He knows how to structure a workout properly so you warm up really well, not just a hurry up couple minute warm up. Then he does a GOOD long stretch to fully stretch you. YOU WILL SWEAT! This is the only workout DVD I've tried where I'm dripping sweat in a short period of time. And I've tried lots of them! You have to be able to shower right after because it will look like you got doused with water when you're done.

He is so motivating and the way the workout is structured you don't get bored. I start thinking about peeling wallpaper with nearly every workout DVD I have after a little while. These workouts are so challenging and they really require you to focus on form and what you're doing, so you can't zone out.

You see the people on the workout taking breaks so you don't feel like a loser when you have to stop and catch your breath.

The diet program is great too. It's really similar to the Zone, but with a bit more carbs. I have food allergies and there is a complete food substitution list, so you can do the diet easily even if you can't eat dairy, wheat or whatever. I've been tracking my calories with the Bodybugg but been unsuccessful for the past 6 weeks of a plateau. On the Insanity diet, I'm full and not hungry at all but I'm eating way less calories. I lost a pound after only 3 workouts!

This work-out product is both effective and incredibly well designed. Not only does the system itself deliver everything it promises (as long as you do YOUR part) it comes with some of the most beautiful and well organized materials I have ever seen.

The case looks like an expensive coffee table book , complete with large faux pages covered in beautiful glossy photos of the exercises. These double as very clever section dividers to the disks. A sturdy pocket in the back of the "book" houses your calendar, fitness test card, recipe book and nutritional guide.

All this flash isn't required for a great exercise program, but since the program itself is exceptional, it is a nice bonus that the production quality and materials hold up to the same standard.

summary: Best use of your workout time
text:
I will keep this short and sweet. Insanity is the BEST cardio, strength, and endurance workout I have tried by far. This workout is incredibly difficult and is designed to push you to your personal limits. You will sweat like you never have before and your muscles will burn like they never have before...two things that often do not happen in the same workout.

About myself: I am a 25 year old woman in good shape who did not desire to get "buff." I wanted a great workout to make me sweat and get me TONED. Insanity's intensity will allow you to burn fat and get toned. I honestly didn't think I had much weight to lose and thought I was pretty fit and toned starting out, but this workout changed my body in ways I was not expecting. In fact, I quit my gym! (And I used to go to my gym 5+ times a week!)

Pros:
- Excellent cardio workout
- Excellent strength and muscle toning workout
- Variety of DVDs in the package to choose from (you won't get bored)
- Don't have to drive (or pay for a gym membership)
- Time saving (most workouts are only 40 minutes)
- Package has two "rest" workouts for days when you do not feel up to it...(these are harder than most normal workouts!)
- Can complete in a very small space
- Can complete a 60 day program for maximum results or simply do the workouts when you have time
- No equipment necessary

Cons: (Hard because I really believe this is the best workout DVD collection out there)
- Takes motivation to complete
- Extremely difficult (not best for beginners)
- Lots of plyometrics (jumping) that may cause injury without proper warmup

In short, please believe me. This is the best workout I have EVER done. I have tried Body by Jake, Jackie Warner, Jillian Michaels (all of the DVDs), and pretty much everything on Time Warner On Demand. This is the real deal. Do yourself a favor and try it. You will not be sorry!

This workout is definitely everything it's hyped up to be...insanity.  My wife and I have been completing the workouts day by day and we're still hanging in there after 3 weeks.  I highly recommend this product if you're healthy enough and able to stretch properly before and after each workout.

I've been into fitness for most of my life, but this series really takes it to a new level.  If you're looking to get into shape before you buy it, my advice is to keep jumping in the air, running in place, and doing squat thrusts.  Then you'll be ready, but the first week will still hurt!  After that your muscles adjust, and you really do see improvement.  I recommend also buying a heart rate monitor so you can see your calorie burn.  Some people can burn 700 calories, I'm a smurf so I only burn 300 per session.  Reality check!
I really enjoyed this workout. I dont really follow the directions, but it def. spices up the workout rotine and works muscles I didnt realize needed working!

summary: Great if you got good knees
text: Great video, workouts are challanging and if you have bad knees you will be hurting, i do, i did it, i moved at my own pace, i still got good scores on my test. it works very well. the only problem i have is they dont give you enough recovery time. so your still sore as a dickens for a week and expcted to workout again the next day. but if you can handle it, stick with it, it will work. good luck. oh! and the video tells yo that if you have bad knees dont do it befor the excersises start.

I love the work out, I haven't been through all the DVD's yet. One of the DVD's does seem to be scratched though, I continuously stops and waits a minute before restarting.  This is very annoying, but I do love the workout. It kicks my butt every time.
The beach body site offers an option for $9.99 that if any of the dvd gets damaged they will replace that particular one. I am not sure if amazon offers that feature.

This dvd selection and workout is not for everyone.  It is very hard and very fast paced.  Even some of the people demonstating the video could not complete the workout.  They focus on repetition as fast as possible.  This doesn't make sense to me because I have always been taught to focus on form so that you don't get hurt. There is no way to keep your form in these workouts.  Very expensive!

Very intense, no nonsense 60-day workout program. Being a 2 time P90X graduate, I hate running and I wanted to lose some more body fat, thus I needed to do more cardio. Like P90X, Insanity fits my needs perfectly. I can do everything from home, on my own time and Shaun T keeps you motivated. I'm currently doing a P90X\Insanity hybrid, P90X 3 times a week and Insanity twice a week. My only complaint about Insanity is that the warmup part of it is kind of long, so much that it's necessary for me to stretch even before I do the warmup. Also, some of the routines in the DVD's are kind of repetitive. Program definitely is geared towards the more advanced exercise enthusiasts, though you can of course always modify. All in all, you will find that this is an exceptionally challenging, high intense cardio calorie burning program. You will sweat buckets and you will see results if you stick with it, just start out slow if necessary at first and take extra breaks.

summary: A Good Workout for the Motivated
text:
This is an excellent workout, as long as you are motivated. Of course, that goes for any exercise! There is enough variation from day to day that it doesn't get too old, and by the time it DOEs (about the 4th week) the workout adds new videos anyways, and so everything changes.

Pros: Can be done at home, with NO needed accessories (except maybe a pad or carpet for when doing ab exercises). They are relatively short, can be done any time throughout the day, and as long as one tries throughout the video, one will be tired at the end of it. I am only on week 4 as of now, and I can run circles around the "3-weeks ago me".
Also:

1. With the videos, it is easy to start the workout before you can talk yourself out of it.

2. You can also turn the music off, and play your own classical or country or whatever motivates you. Personally, I kept the music that they gave, as it wasn't too bad.

3.They also have a nutrition booklet, which I suppose is a pro if you use it. I am too lazy to spend the time figuring that all out, and figure I eat all right as it is.

4. If you don't do the videos in order, or just plain skip one because you're too busy, the workout is built so that each day is (essentially) everything. While there are different focuses for each video, each workout will work all your muscles no matter what, so missing a day will not leave some muscles behind.

Cons: The calendar that comes with the workout is a little confusing, as they don't label the videos correctly on a few days. But after a little process of elimination, that's easily solved.

Also, for those of you with bad knees or feet, this is probably not the video for you. There is a lot of jumping and knee lifting.

So: If you are the type of person who doesn't mind exercise, but wants to get in shape REALLY fast, I can recommend this video. I am currently getting ready for boot camp, and needed something that I could stick with easily (the do it from home part) but still push me to my limits. I feel confidant that by the time I leave, I will be ahead of many of my peers. I am not even at the halfway point and I can say this. For me, it was worth the 100 bucks--what you might spend on a gym that you only go to whenever you get around to it. However, if you are not in very good shape, going to the gym for a while or simply walking or running in the morning may be a good thing to do before starting this, as it...well...insane.

First point...If you are deciding between P90x and this go for P90x. I've done p90x a few times with great results and this workout mixed with P90x is fun too. That's why i'm giving it 3 stars. I'm not going to give a 4 or 5 star rating just because the workouts kicked my butt. If you are looking for something different and liked P90x then make the call....if you don't like push ups and plyo you better keep on looking.

I just finished the complete workout for the first time following the calendar exactly. The 2nd month workouts are hard and long...I really never felt like I recovered. By the end of each week in month 2 I was wasted. Always hungry and always tired. I was already in pretty good shape so could keep up but felt like the intensity was so high (in month 2) that by the end of the week I was suffering more than moving forward. I also gained weight and lost muscle mass in my arms and abs that I had gained in P90x. I did thicken up in my chest from the daily round of push ups and made some gains in my legs from the plyo.

If you like push ups, jumping, and BB drills then this set is for you. Don't come back and review until you've done it all....not just the first couple of weeks (there easy)....Also if you have a busy schedule then it will be tough to do these workouts and work a 8-10 hour a day job....unless you get paid to eat and sleep.
If you throw up, you're doing it right. LOL. AMAZING program! 10 lbs in first 8 days! VERY intense! You'll laugh, you'll cry, you'll trim ur back side!

I'm officially obsessed! One of the best at home workouts out there. If you workout from home a lot like I do (the Firm, the Jillian, etc) then this is the next step for you when all of those DVDs are getting way too easy.

I started the program on Sept 20th and while I have not lost the weight I though I would, I've lost more inches then I could have imagined. Four inches in less than a month. If you are looking for a workout that will push your limits and leave you gasping for breath, but cause you to feel stronger, more alive, and more active, this is the one. Not good for you if you have never worked out, but if it's been a few years and you need a sharp kick in the rear, Shawn T will give it to you.

I just received my Insanity package (ordered through Amazon), opened it up and there are no CD's!!!!!!!!!!!!

What a waste of time. Obviously no quality control program for who packages this together. Duh.
Showed up in the condition that the seller stated it was in. Could not be happier.

Really enjoying this workout.  This is my first time to do a DVD workout, and I was worried I wouldn't get much out of it.  After 3 weeks, people are noticing a difference in how I look.  Just ran a half marathon, and due to my improved cardiovascular state, was able to take 5 minutes off my PR.  I wish I was better about following the diet plan, that would probably really drop the pounds.  But as it is, I am definitely more toned and have improved stamina.  Terrific!

summary: Nice, Fast Pace With A Great Overall Plan
text:
After completing P90X, I decided to try Insanity. These two programs are probably by far the best DVD workout programs on the market. The biggest difference I have noticed is that Insanity is done at a much faster pace. There are breaks after every four or six workouts like in P90X, but the big difference is that Shaun T doesn't TALK for 15-30 seconds between each workout. It's a non-stop thing, and you have to pick it up on the fly. That might make for a short learning curve the first time through, but it also makes for a MUCH better cardiovascular workout than P90X. I like the difference though. Insanity is great for cutting weight and improving cardiovascular performance, while its sister product, P90X, can build a little muscle.

This workout gets a 5 from me though. It is well thought out with different techniques and a much more random schedule than P90X. I wish I could write a review for both at once rather than compare them here, but I think most people wanting a review on Insanity would either be familiar with P90X or be comparing it to P90X before making a purchase. I bought mine on eBay though - $70-80 over there for the full box with 13 DVDs, eating guide, and schedule/fit test tracker vs $140+ from Amazon right now.

This item was exactly as promised. Came in original packaging and included everything as promised, such as wall calendar and bonus dvds. We've been doing this workout for almost a month now and the results have been amazing!!
The shipping did take wayyy longer than expected which was somewhat disappointing because we wanted to get started asap. However, once it got here we've been very pleased (and sore!)
Love this DVD series.  It's tough, but it keeps you engaged and really challenges you to work hard.  I really like the variety.  If you stick with it, it really gets you in shape!

I couldn't be happier with this product! i have had such amazing results with it. i wish i would have known about this sooner! I'm almost done with my 60 days...one week left and i have lost 15 lbs and i don't even know how many inches total yet...but at least 3 pants sizes! my next purchase is going to be hip hop abs...i love Shaun T! all i can say is: "order it! you won't regret it!"

summary: First program that worked for me
text:
I've struggled my whole life to find an exercise program that actually improved my fitness but at the same time improved how I looked. I've joined gyms but lost interest when I got bored. I've bought a few different exercise devices, including expensive cross trainers and bikes. None of them did much, even though I would stick with them for years. I think one big problem is that the time commitment was vague. I would go to the gym, but toward what goal? Losing inches? Losing weight? Gaining inches? Insanity is great because it is a commitment of 60 days. Then you either see results or don't.

Insanity is the first program that has worked for me. I've lost fat and gained muscle.

There are many great things about the program. Here are a few:

The program includes a list of foods that are going to help you achieve your goals of looking better. The foods are on tiers, basically lists. Avocados, bananas and blueberries are tier 1, meaning really good for you. But there are one hundred more, including meats, carbs, etc. on tier 1. I've eaten more bananas in the past 40 days than in my whole life. Oh...and by the way, for the first time in my life I am drinking no soda-because the program is only 60 days, I told myself I was going to make this commitment. So just try to find foods and snacks that are on tier 1 or Tier 2. Tier 2, are foods that are good for you. Tier 3 are foods that are sort of neutral, and then tiers 4 and 5 are foods you should stay away from. Important is that it is all really simple, and that some things, like yogurt, are good for you if they are low fat, no sugar, etc. But are not if they have these things. Sweet potatoes are good. Regular potatoes not. It's a quick way to make sure you are eating the right stuff. If you eat junk, no amount of exercise is going to get you where you want to be.

The program can be a lifetime commitment, but...it's really just sixty days. I'm at day 40 and I have seen really good, almost amazing results. So, instead of some vague, "I'm going to go to the gym more" promise. You commit to 60 days and do it. Tell your friends, family, work, whatever, that sorry...I can't do X thing today, I've got to work out. Or sure, I'll go on that trip, but I need an hour a day to do this routine.

The program is on DVDs. No equipment is necessary besides maybe a carpeted floor. If you have a DVD player, or a computer, you're good to go. So if you travel, it's no problem. This was great for me. I've brought the DVDs on vacations, on work trips, etc.

For the first 30 days, most of the routines are just over 30 minutes. Not bad. So exercise shower and all in less than an hour. After the first 30 days, the exercises get longer. But by then, you should be seeing results, and you will justify going longer.

I won't go on, I know a lot of the other reviews say about the same thing. In a nutshell, Shaun and the Insanity crew have created a really good exercise program but one that also includes some great suggestions about how to manage your diet which is also key. I hope they are really successful with it.

summary: So challenging even Shaun T has to take a break every now and then!!
text: I am finishing up my third week of this nine week workout program and I can already tell a major difference in the way my body feels. I'm definitely stronger and my cardiovascular strength has greatly improved. INSANITY is extremely challenging and you definitely know it is when Shaun T has to stop to take a break and the people working out in the background stop mid-exercise to catch their breath or get water....that never happens in workout videos! I am very happy with INSANITY so far! My goal is to complete the program in its entirety! Only 6.5 weeks to go.
This is an excellent workout, but I would not recommend it for beginners because I think they will get intimidated and quit the program.

I have done the P90X program before this, so I thought that the insanity workout would be easier for me...but boy was I wrong. It really is intense and works out every muscle in your body. I was also going to the gym 5 times a week, but even the fit test (which is their intro workout) was hard for me!

One thing that I would say is better with the P90X program is that they have 3 different people showing examples of certain intensities. So at first, you could follow the easier example then progress at your own pace, which is a lot safer and you get more accurate workouts because you perfect your form before you advance to higher intensities. Right out of the gate with insanity, they drill you to go hard and fast. So, for the first week, my back was in bad shape because I was trying to match their intensity without focusing on how well I was performing each exercise.

Needless to say, it is a great cardio workout. If you are looking to lose weight and improve your cardio, this would be your product. I would suggest P90X for more strength training.

summary: I thought I was in shape until Shaun T kicked my butt
text:
This isn't for the faint of heart. You need an exercise area, sneakers, water and a big towel because this workout will make you sweat.

I would consider myself "in shape". My gym closed down for 3 months for renovations and I do have a personal trainer. But my wife and I needed some cardio because it's getting to cold to run outside. So decided to get Insanity.

We previewed the DVD and bought some workout mats that were thick enough not to damage our joints and move out all the boxes in the basement to clear enough space for the workout also. During the first "fit test", I nearly lost vomited. Dripping in sweat and drinking almost half a gallon of water. My wife (who is in better shape than I am) was whining in pain.

I'm on day 4 now and days 1-3 were tough. Neither of us can walk without something hurting and stairs are tough. LOL. I'm in pain as I type this review! It is worth it, you need to be dedicated and have about 45 mins/day. I'm looking forward to the second fit test in 10 days!

best workout ever. it got me sweating even when it was cold outside. if you are a mom who is busy all the time, buy this.. it only takes like 30 minutes to completed it
great workout buy it, trust me you will love like i do.

This program is great.  The workouts are a challenge but the way I feel after is worth it.  I have not yet completed my insanity workout 8 week program.  I am about to start week 5(recovery week) and I feel great!  I have lost 15 pounds!  I am so happy I decided to purchase insanity, best money ive spent in a while!

They don't call it Insanity because it's easy. This really is the hardest workout system ever put on DVD. Just a little background about my fitness level. . . . I have been a personal trainer for about 15 years and working out even longer. You name it, I've tried it. I run marathons, am a big fan of spinning, and have even done a few rounds of P90X (which I love btw!!!) I figured I'd try this to get a little leaner during the summer months because I don't like to run in the heat. I was impressed by how comprehensive the system is. The food guide is much easier to understand than the P90X eating plan.
So I started with the "Fitness Test" DVD and thought I was going to die!!! I was so embarassed. I couldn't believe how much I sucked at this workout. But never one to back down from a challenge I kept coming back for more day after day. Let me just tell you, for the first couple of weeks, my heart rate got into the 170's just during the warm up!!! There were many times I was grabbing my knees and heaving for breath, but then I'd look up at the video, and see some of the participants doing the very same thing!!
For those of you who work out for an hour or so a day, you will probably find the first 30 days doesn't feel like enough of a workout (the workouts are about 30-40 mins). I supplemented it with additional cardio like spinning for another 30 minutes. The second 30 days really kicks it up a notch, and was more than enough of a workout. These workouts last about 48-55 minutes. I was so tired at the end of them, the last thing I wanted to do was workout some more.
As the weeks passed, I was more comfortable with the workouts, and was amazed with the transformation in my body and the increase in my fitness level. Like one of the other reviewers stated, you do lose a little of the size in your "glamour muscles" (back and biceps), but the definition in my shoulders, legs, and abs just popped! According to the scale my body fat hasn't decreased, but my pants are much roomier, and people have been asking what I have been doing to lose so much weight. But to be honest, my eating could have been a little better during the program. I have started running again and training for my next marathon. I cannot believe how much easier running is now that I have completed Insanity. I know its the perfect supplement for runners. The exercises really work your core and improve your speed.
Buy this workout program!!! You will not regret it!

Great product if you like cardio. Im a p90x grad and im 4 weeks into my 2nd round. Honestly If your looking to bulk up do some kind of hybrid with insanity and p90x. This program is more about losing weight and toning up. Would recommend a heart rate monitor with this one. This program will push you to your limits cardio wise

summary: If you thought plyometrics on p90x was hard....
text: Like the previous reviewer, I have done both p90x and Insanity. I have come to the conclusion that for me, a combination of the two is the way to go. It all depends what your goals are. p90x alternates between lifting weights/doing pull ups and push ups with cardio. You focus on a couple of muscle groups during each workout, do the same weekly routine for a month, then switch to different exercises for a month. The last month is the original set of exercises again. If you're looking to build muscle, this is definitely the better option. It requires dumbbells or bands, a pull up bar, and a chair. The cardio portions are good, with plyometrics being relatively difficult. It also includes a day of Yoga, which Tony Horton loves but I personally could not do.  Insanity is a whole different animal. It is, in my opinion, more intense than p90x, but is focused on improving your cardiovascular stamina using max interval training. You have to be in pretty good shape to start to actually finish a workout at their pace. You can think of it as a shorter but much more intense version of plyometrics everyday. It doesn't require any equipment at all - just using your own body weight to get results. Most workouts are less than 30 mins. I found doing this daily was too much for my knees but this may not be the case for you. I have started alternating p90x with Insanity, eliminating the p90x leg workout since Insanity really works your legs. Both products are high quality and should get you results if you stick with them. Highly recommended.

summary: I would give it a 10 out of 5 if I could!
text:
Other reviewers have really gone into detail about the Insanity program, the breakdown of each workout and what to expect out of it so I'm just going to write a review about the impact that this program has had on my life.

I'm a 29 year old, active female that's been working out since I was 18. My favorite types of workouts are the kind that either involve a lot of jumping (plyometrics, step, jump rope) or the kind that make you wanna hurl (sprints, spinning, burpees) - or both! This workout definitely involves both. I did my first round of Insanity in January of 2010. Like other reviewers, I agreed that this was the hardest workout video I'd ever done. After the first warm-up, I hurled and at that point I knew I'd forever love this workout.

As of today I've finished 4 cycles of Insanity (not all back-to-back, and the last 2 times were done interspersed with weight-training), and it never gets "easier", which is a great thing. Going from month 1 to month 2, I still experience that sense of fear that you only get before doing a really hard workout. During the first cycle, I lost 25 lbs (though I had put on 30 lbs when I relocated from Toronto to California - which I'm sure had everything to do with my new "American" diet and little to do with exercise, which I still did religiously). I can't say that the program itself was the source of all my weight loss because when I started the Insanity program I simultaneously went back to my normal eating habits (clean eating, and no junk food), but the physical change I experienced was enough to turn a lot of heads. So many people noticed the difference in my weight and fitness level that after I finished my first cycle, 7 of my friends bought the Insanity program and became addicts themselves.

I really like Shaun T in this series, too. In hip-hop abs, I felt he was lacking in the masculinity department. In this series, everyone in the DVD looks like an athlete and you can see that they all work at their own pace - they really push, but also still need to take breaks.
