As a P90X graduate, I was looking forward to burning off a little more goo from around my midsection, so I decided that Insanity was the way to go. In some ways, I was right. In others, I was wrong.

Insanity is a program created around the idea of "Max Interval Training." For those who don't know, in a typical interval you would do a move for one minute total; it would be done slowly for 30-45 seconds, and quickly for the final amount of time, allowing plenty of rest in between the fast segments. This allows your heart rate to go up and down, gives your body a chance to recover, etc... In Insanity, this formula is turned upside down. You go fast and hard for extended periods of time with short rests in between. A typical workout consists of three sets of four moves, each done three times, plus a warm up/cool down section.

It is important to note that the demands this type of workout puts on your body is extremely high. You'll be jumping, planting, pushing, squatting, flailing, and struggling throughout the entire workout, but as Shaun T repeatedly says, take breaks when you need them. If your form starts to go south, back off and get it back together. Make absolutely sure that you have a high quality pair of shoes (I use New Balance cross trainers), and a solid surface to do your workouts on (I work on a cement floor covered with a half inch of foam rubber with carpet on top). This workout is EXTREMELY HIGH IMPACT. Those with potential knee/shin/hip problems need to look elsewhere.

This really can't be compared with P90X at all. One is based mainly on weight training... the other on cardio/bodyweight exercises. Interestingly enough, I lost 25 pounds during the course of P90X. Throughout my sixty days of Insanity, I didn't lose one pound. Other people say they've lost a lot of weight doing this program. I didn't. I followed the diet plan, never missed a workout, and worked myself to exhaustion every day, and I didn't lose one pound. I'm not complaining, because my body looks much better... it's tighter, I've turned quite a bit of fat into lean muscle, and I'm quite a bit more flexible. So I did accomplish my goal of getting rid of some goo. It just didn't show itself on the scale. That was my experience... I'm not saying this program isn't for weight loss, I'm saying that it didn't cause me to lose weight. Take that with a grain of salt.

*****IMPORTANT EDIT*********

I just realized the main reason why I may have not lost any weight doing this plan. When I was following the diet tips, I unknowingly was consuming enough calories in order to "Maintain My Current Weight." According to the plan, I should have been subtracting 500 calories per day from my meals. So, if you're doing Insanity and not losing weight, make sure you are taking in the correct amount of calories.
********END EDIT***********

This program has a very strict divide between month one and month two. Month one merely prepares you for the rigors that month 2 brings. Each month has a workout that corresponds with one from the other month... sort of like a simple/advanced relationship (despite the fact that simple isn't simple). They break down as such...

Cardio Intervals
Month 1: Plyometric Cardio Circuit
Month 2: Max Interval Circuit

Both of these workouts involve a wide variety of jumping and endurance moves. Month two adds 15 seconds to each move (so the intervals are three minutes long instead of two) and a longer, tougher warm up.

Plyometric Strength Intervals
Month 1: Cardio Power and Resistance
Month 2: Max Interval Plyo

Get ready for some push ups! These two will really have your shoulders and arms on fire, not to mention your legs and back. These are probably the best full body workouts.

Cardio and Endurance
Month 1: Pure Cardio
Month 2: Max Cardio Conditioning

Pure Cardio was a slap in the face to me. It was 20 minutes of constant exercises... no rests. Max Cardio Conditioning expanded on this. It was about 15 minutes longer, still no rests, but there are recovery moves thrown in.

Recovery Workouts
Month 1: Cardio Recovery
Month 2: Max Recovery

Wait, these are recovery workouts? These are tough! Particularly Max Recovery... it will really stretch out and strengthen your core and shoulders. Despite their difficulty, they do give your heart a much needed rest.

Abdominal Workouts
Month 1: Cardio Abs
Month 2: Insane Abs (only included in "Deluxe" version)

Cardio Abs is probably the easiest workout in the whole bunch (and also the shortest). Insane Abs is about 2x as long, and it is by far, the best, most enjoyable ab workout I've ever done. It blows P90X's Ab Ripper X out of the water in every way possible. If you can get a hold of Insane Abs, I would highly recommend it.

The two other workouts I haven't mentioned are Core Cardio and Balance (a pseudo-recovery workout that blends everything together *the last 5 minutes are brutal!!*) and Max Interval Sports Training... a "Deluxe" package workout that incorporates moves with various sports in mind.

Just a quick word about the two "Deluxe" workouts... I borrowed them from a friend of mine, and they ended up being my two favorite workouts. Get a hold of them if you can. There is a third deluxe workout called Upper Body Weight Training, but I never tried it.

In conclusion, this workout has a 30 day money back guarantee for a reason. If you can't make it through the first 30 days, there's no way you'll make it through the second 30. But if you're in good shape and are looking for something to really push the envelope, you've really got nothing to lose other than some inches (and possibly some muscle mass unless you incorporate weight training).

As for me, I'm not sure if I'll do another complete Insanity cycle. It seems like something you do once and then move on to something else. It would seem odd to me to start back with month 1 after the month 2 workouts are so unbelievably taxing. I think I'm going back to P90X and P90X+ in order to put back some of the upper body muscle mass that Insanity took off.

Have fun, and don't give up!

summary: I love it...but you better be ready!
text:
I bought Insanity because I needed a new challenge. I have been doing videos from "The Firm", Tae Bo, and other really popular videos for years, and started to get a little bored with the routine. I had seen an infomercial for Insanity once at night, and I thought, "It CAN'T be that hard." Never one to back down from a fitness challenge, I decided to go for it. As a former collegiate athlete, I figured I would be able to do at least at much as those in the workout...WRONG! From the fit test, I knew I was in for a workout circuit like I've never seen before. The first time I did the Fit Test, I was nearly embarrassed that I could get as many reps as I thought I could with the exercises! But that was just the beginning. From the first workout, I started thinking, "What the f*$& have I gotten myself into?!?!?" But that was just fear and doubt playing tricks on me, and I made a decision right then and there that I wasn't gonna quit this program, I don't care how many breaks I have to take. Other reviewers are absolutely correct...the participants in the video are taking breaks just like you, so don't feel bad! I just did my 2nd fit test to kick off week 3, and I did substantially better this go-round than I did the first time I did it. My weight loss hasn't been lightning fast...just the recommended amount (i.e. 2-3 pounds a week), but have already lost a few inches around my body. But to do this workout, you MUST, YOU MUST eat and drink AT LEAST 8 glasses of water daily...other than that, you won't have the energy to even think about Insanity.

Now for the disclaimers...if you have anything wrong with any joint of your arms, shoulders, or any part of your lower half, this IS NOT the workout for you, because it will probably most definitely aggrevate whatever condition it is. Also, do what YOU can do, because probably 9 times out of 10, you won't be able to keep up with those in the video. Push as hard as you can, but know your own limits. Don't get down on yourself at first, because if you stick with it, you will see a change in your fitness...there's no getting worse with this workout.

Lastly, make sure you get some kind of recovery formula. I didn't get the one that is advertised within the Insanity DVDs (it's just a little too expensive for me), but I did go to GNC and get an amino acid recovery formula to use both during and after my workouts, and it has nearly eliminated the soreness so that I can move around the next day and it has helped with my stamina during the workouts.

Take a chance and go for it! Get INSANE!!!

text: I've completed 3 rounds of P90X, 1 round of P90X+, 2 rounds of Billy Banks TB boot camp, and Insanity is the hardest cardio workout I've ever done. To gain strength and power, you need to do P90X or lift on your own.  You can only get so strong doing pushups and floor dips.  Yet as for pure cardio, you can't beat this program.  As a benchmark; if you struggle with Plyometrics in P90X, this program with totally smoke you.  It's a great program and worth checking out for all of us home fitness folks. summary: Good for your heart, bad for your knees.
text: My sister had the Insanity DVD's and I absolutely loved borrowing them from her.  I decided to get my own set and start the 60 day program.  The workouts are great and work almost all of your muscle groups while keeping you moving constantly.  Despite my love for this program, I did have to stop after 2 weeks due to the severe straining of my knees.  I ignored the warnings from other users about knee injuries... DO NOT USE if you have any knee issues.  I'm only 22, but have had an ACL tear and knee surgery 5 years ago. summary: The Iron Man of fitness videos
text:
There's 300 reviews on these excercise videos so I'll cut straight to the chase with my observations:

1.) Don't get this if you have joint problems or if you're seriously obese. Ditto if you have heart problems of any kind or if you're diabetic. I'm no doctor or trainer, but this will push your body to the limit so apply common sense. This program 100% lives up to its namesake, its not just a marketing ploy.

2.) If you're not in shape or are simply quite a bit overweight, expect the adjustment curve to severe. I mean like crashing mid-way through a workout the first one or two times, and having to sit down. I've also taken a half hour nap directly after finishing a routine more than once I was so wiped. There is no build up for newbies, and this was a bit of a shock for me as I was 50 pounds overweight. I did 500 calorie a workout cardio(eliptical and treadmill) 4 times a week for two weeks leading up to this and I was still leveled in the first video.

3.) If you're new or even just not a fitness junkie, buy yourself a basic heart rate monitor and figure out how to pace yourself or you'll experience crashes per number 2 above. The Polar RS100 is perfect for that. Nothing is more disappointing than having to stop half way through because you over did it early on.

4.) You hear this all the time, but this workout regimen makes it absolutely critical. Drink lots of fluids every day, put some simple sugars and electrolytes in your body before(to not crash) and after(to recover) workouts, and always do the stretching to the best of your ability during the video.

5.) If you lose form, stop, take a breather, and start over. Losing form puts you at serious risk of straining a muscle which you may or may not notice at the time because you're so exhausted and you're endorphins are pumping. If a muscle or joint seriously hurts(not just tired or sore), stop immediately and stop doing the videos till it gets better.

6.) This workout will get you lean throughout and build your endurance and lower body power, but it won't build your upper body.

7.) I have to say is it's killer hard to keep at it. I have stopped and restarted many times. I find getting through week one in its entirety is the roughest and it gradually gets better from there, although never any easier. Talk about sore.

8.) Month 2 is ridiculous. We're talking doubling the workout length and intensity. One month simply isn't enough for most people to prepare for that kind of abuse. I'm not sure if I'll ever be motivated enough to take it on to be honest. Month 1 is still kicking my butt.

Hope this helps set everyone expectations. These videos certainly aren't cheap, but they are unique. Shaun T is good about pointing out good(and bad) form and reminding everyone to break as needed, and the workouts are a great challenge for people that thrive on that.

As far as results, the jury is still out for me but its definitely working fast. I will update this review after another month.

summary: LOVE this workout but watch your achilles tendon!
text:
Overall, I am very happy with the intensity of this workout. I started with P90X, which I also like a lot, but found that it didn't have enough cardio to effect weight loss. I was getting stronger, but my clothes were also getting a bit tighter.

So I switched to Insanity, and within a week I noticed a difference in how my clothes were fitting. I did feel that the total amount of cardio time in the first phase was a little short, so I added on about 15 minutes of treadmill walking after the workout to stretch out my muscles and cool down a bit more.

When I first started the program, I was a little surprised that there was a super intense wind-sucking warm-up with jumping before there was any stretching. After ten minutes of madness, then you stop cold and stretch.

A few days ago, I noticed that I was expereincing discomfort in my achilles tendon. I tried to stretch it, and work through it, but it just got worse after every workout. When I couldn't walk without limping (after 3 days) I finally went to see a doctor, who diagnosed tendonitis. She said it probably happened from doing plyometric work on a cold tendon.

So now I have to take several days off and hope it resolves.

That being said, I cannot wait to resume the workout BUT I will make sure that I do a light warm up myself first, and then thoroughly stretch myself out before starting the warm up. I think with this precaution I can safely continue the workouts.

I highly recommend this system for expereinced exercisers, but PLEASE take the time to do a little pre warm-up so you don't find yourself benched due to achilles tendon pain.

If you are willing to work hard and sweat you will see results.  I lost 10 pounds in 3 weeks just got into the second set of workouts and it steps you up to a brand new level.  The fit tests will keep you motivated doubled most of my scores from the first to the second tests.  Shows how quickly you can change and evolve your fitness to the next level.  I did give it 4 stars just because it is extremely challenging and would love a next step after the 60 days.  Such as a calendar to mix up all of the workouts after the 60 days to keep you going.  Or an opportunity to get additional videos once a month to mix into a routine.  Totally worth it but you have to be willing to do the work.

summary: Rrrrrripppp....yes, that was the sound of my abs flexing
text:
This is a nuts set of workout DVD's. I am overweight and just shy of 40, but I have dreams of getting back into my pre-marriage body. I decided to seize the day and go for it, and I am not sorry. My muscles are currently screaming, every bit of me hurts. Every day, I both love and dread pushing play on this dvd, because I know what will happen when I do. I will spend 45 minutes gasping, lurching around, heart pounding, sweat running off me like a monsoon, desparately trying to keep up with a workout designed by fitness demigods. Afterwards, when I can catch my breath and pull myself up of the ground, I feel so good it is not even funny. Yesterday when I finished my workout and was talking to my wife, I said "You know what I feel like? I feel like I'm on vacation!". You know, that feeling you get on day 1 of vacation when you have the whole thing stretching before you, when there is a cool drink in your hands and not a care in the world? That's how I feel when my blood is pumping, when my body is sore and I am so proud of myself.

I can't even begin to keep up with this video, but that is ok. I keep my heart rate up, I have a great time, and I try to get a little better every day. I'm not done with the program yet, I hope I have the stamina to keep it up, but for now, this is fantastic.

The DVD's themselves are good, the music is fine, the instructor is incredible and never demeaning. I feel like he is speaking directly to me and he is very encouraging. I am also encouraged when the folks exercising with him can't keep up, because I know that if these very in shape people can't do it, then I am in good company. The rest of the package is fine. I'm on weight watchers, so I'm not using their eating plan. I'm not changing diets midstream. Anyway, the workout calendar is nice, I keep it up to date and it is a good motivational tool for me. The DVD case is compact and sturdy. It's a little pricey, but I think that it is worth it so far. It is giving me back my self respect.

----**UPDATE**
I've done the program now for 21 days. I have gone down 2 pant sizes, lost 11 pounds, am losing my love handles, have had to take my belt in 2 notches (almost 3!) and am getting my neck back! The workouts are very active. They are very intense, and the more I do them, the more intense they can get. When I first started, I could not do the exercises with anything approaching good form. 3 weeks on, my form has improved, but now the workouts are tougher because I'm pushing myself harder to complete them. Shaun T. is inspirational,and I have a love hate relationship with him on the DVDs! I yell at the screen as I exercise. Get yourself a good pair of shoes, it made a huge difference to me, and make sure you do all the warm ups. If you are chunky like me when you start, don't be discouraged, just keep at it, do your best, and so far the results have made me a believer. It has been a very hard 3 weeks, but I love the way I feel, I'm happy to be in clothes I thought I would never wear again, and my wife and co-workers all notice the difference. This set has made a big difference in my attitude towards exercise, and I think I'm going to do P90x when Insanity is done!

--**Update**
Day 31 of insanity here, down 14.1 pounds, ran 5k yesterday, pushing harder. The workouts don't get easier, but there is a huge sense of accomplishment every day as I fill in the workout calendar. Someone told me today that I look thinner, and I was very excited. I'm still thick, don't get me wrong, but I'm getting there. Insanity has made me excited to get physical.

--**Update**
5 weeks of insanity done, 17 pounds down, preparing for a 4.5 mile run this weekend, really nervous about starting week 6--it supposedly gets even insaner (?). My wife has joined me for some of the workouts and my kids are now doing it with me (as much as they are able, and they have a great time!)--the whole family has gotten into it. Can't say enough about how good I feel--it is a crime to feel this good, I swear.

--**Update**
I must admit that I look forward to these little updates, as I use them for encouragement. Anyway, day 45 of insanity is today. From a discipline standpoint, this is a daily decision--these workouts are hard. I feel great, but every day, I look in the mirror and think a)this is great and b)long way to go. On the up side, my belt is too big, have to use it on its tightest setting. I'm down 18.5 pounds since I began. I can see my neck--and it is not just a solid column of blubber. I have abs popping out (!) (although they are still buried under some belly fat--let's face it, I started this waaaay overweight). My wife has now joined the culture of fitness in our family, and is working out regularly. The second month of insanity, which starts 6 weeks in, is significantly more insane than the first month (which I didn't think was humanly possible). Shaun T goes completely nuts, and the workouts are tougher, more intense, longer, and still lots of fun. I could never have dreamed 45 days ago of keeping up this level of activity. Back on day 1, the first warm up blew me away and I wanted to lay down and cry. Now, the warm up still kicks my rear end, but I know it is because I am trying HARDER working STRONGER doing Better. My flexibility is so much increased! I walk around and I feel stronger in everything that I do. Listen folks, this is a great program. If you have the determination, it will change you, mentally, physically, cardiovascularly. It is so hard, but soooooo good.

--**Update**
Today is day 59 of Insanity. Wow. I can't believe I have almost made it through the first round. I weighed myself today, and I am down 21.8 pounds. My old pants are falling off me--literally. I put them on yesterday just to walk around the house because they were in the top of the "clean" pile, and they fell right off. I had to change clothes! I'm using a smaller belt I never thought I would use again. My size 36 jeans are now my jeans of choice (down from busting out of size 40's to the point that I wouldn't even wear jeans because they were not comfortable). I'm planning on doing Insanity: The Asylum when this round is done, which will turn the Insanity journey into a 90 day (actually, 93) day trip. Then, on to p90x!

--**Update**
This will likely be my final update. I finished Insanity 2 days ago. Wow. Wow. It was a bear. The last week was so intense, I struggled just to keep up (two Max Plyo workouts? Two Max Interval workouts? And Cardio Abs twice??). I'm 22+ pounds down, happy as a clam, sore as can be, and chomping at the bit to keep going. I did my final fit test, and more than doubled many of my exercises--I would NEVER have believed it possible. I was still sucking wind by the end of the fit test, because I was pushing as hard as I could to better my last scores. I started the sequel to this video set (Insanity: The Asylum) yesterday, and it is equally intense, but different. I'll probably review it as well when I have done more of the workouts. Anyway, I could never have survived even 5 minutes of the Asylum if I hadn't done Insanity first.

In the end, this set worked for me because I needed someone to push me. Or I thought I did--I really ended up pushing myself, but the videos gave me the structure and the tools to get it done. I promised myself I would do it every day, even if I had to workout at midnight. It was just me, a pair of shoes, and my DVD player, kicking some butt. Some reservations here--it is not easy on your joints. I'm 40, and overweight. Some exercises were just too hard on my knees, and I modified them. I kept my heart rate up. Shaun always says "exercise at your own level", but what I told myself was "exercise just a little past your level". So I did, and it worked for me. Take their warnings seriously--don't do this if you aren't willing to push, and if you have health concerns, then for heaven's sake, choose something else. But if you are willing to get your goose cooked on a daily basis and come back and ask for seconds (!), then this is a great choice. Cheers to everyone in the Insane Posse of Fitness Gazelles, and I hope that these updates have helped. Be smart, work hard, and whatever method you are using to lose weight, Insanity or something else, keep it up. I'll be doing the same!

--**Update**
I know that I said that the last update would be my last update. But I wanted to give a status report 1 year on--I'm now just shy of 50 lbs down since I began one year ago. I did the following things--I did Insanity x 1 round, Insanity Asylum x 1 round, P90x+Insanity hybrid x 1 round (P90x + insanity cardio), P90x straight up x 1 round, and I'm now in the midst of a p90x2 + Insanity hybrid with 3 weeks to go before completion. I also run 1-2x per week for 45min to 60 min on the elliptical because I enjoy it. I do insanity with a 20 lb weight vest on now sometimes, and I run on the elliptical with a weight vest. I have gone from being able to do 1 (count it, 1!) pull up to 10 sets of 8 pullups. They aren't the prettiest pull ups around, but I get up, all on my own. I can do push ups until the cows come home. I'm still about 20 lbs overweight from what I'd like to be, but I'm not complaining. At 50 lbs in a year, you can see that weight has been slow but steadily coming off. No loose skin, lots and lots of muscle coming on. I'm still a big dude--but I now RUN up and down the stairs at work. And I'm out of breath--but I love it. I'm not yet back in my wedding suit, but I've pulled out clothes I haven't worn in YEARS. Yesterday, I had to take off a sweater because it swallowed me whole. Then I put on another sweater--and it was too big also.

All of this is to say that I haven't done anything that crazy, not really. About an hour a day, sometimes more because I really enjoy it now, sometimes less when I'm tired. I do it 6 days a week when I'm on insanity only, 5 days now on p90x2 because that is the program. I still do weight watchers, and it has changed my relationship with food. I still love to eat (believe me!) but now I eat to enjoy and not to make myself stuffed. I still have a burger and a beer on Friday nights and I don't worry about it. I eat a lot of healthy things, and have discovered that I enjoy them. That's a shock.

I'm just a dude. I have a job, I work 60+ hours a week. I have 3 kids. I have a wife. I have pets. I have a yard. But I decided that no amount of pain during exercise was as painful as not being able to wrestle with my boys. No amount of pain in a workout is as bad as sitting on a couch and feeling gross in my own skin. So I got going. I have to keep struggling every day--some days I just want to sit down and not get up--but then I think of how things were only a year ago, and I think that, yea, I can get off my duff and exercise. The insanity/p90x programs work for me because I respond to structure (I need someone telling me what to do!) and I can't afford a trainer. Shaun and Tony are my trainers now.

You can do it. You really can. I've been super careful--done all the stretches, listened to my body, MODIFY MODIFY MODIFY when I knew that the movements weren't possible for me, and I've by and large avoided major injury. Lots of sore muscles. Shin splints. A few things like that. But just use your good sense--protect your body, give it all your love, and it will love you for it.

You can do it. I'm still doing it. See you 20 lbs down, ok?

--**Update**
Just a quick update, now 16 months after I bought insanity. I'm down another 5 lbs (every pound seems to get harder!) but I have really noticed improvements in my muscles as well. Anyway, the reason for the update is just some personal goals are starting to happen that I never thought I could do. I ran a 5k in honor of a friend who died of cancer. My entire family ran it--my wife, my 3 kids, and I all crossed the finish line. My 5, 6, and 8 year olds were so proud of themselves and I was about to burst with pride. Afterwards, I felt so good that I signed up for a 10k; I ran it last weekend and had my best run ever. I decided to start training for a half marathon, and I am using Insanity/p90x as my cross training days. I've always wanted to run, to be a runner, but I never had the courage. I was afraid that it was going to hurt. That I couldn't do it. But after insanity, I figured that workout aches and pains were just the feeling of my body getting stronger, right? So Here I go! Oh, and I got a bike. Don't look now, but I need to take a swim class...

I'm into week 3, but right away I could tell if I could keep myself "pushing play" everyday I'd have great results. I'm 49 years old, so I haven't pushed myself this hard in a while. I thought I was going to drop over just in the fitness test, but I kept going and I am having positive results. The work out doesn't get any easier, because the more in shape you get, the more you push yourself. summary: Shaun T can't even complete his own workout...
text:
I *like* this workout but it annoys the crap out of me at the same time. I am in my late 30's, working mother of two, trying to get back into shape. As for the positive aspects of this video, the cardio is tough, and overall it is good for the core/butt/lower body. Lots of squats, love it or hate it. OK for abs, and the upper body exercises were too difficult to do. I wish there were modifications with respect to the upper body exercises.

Shaun T. is hella annoying. He refers to himself in the third person. "Shaun T. is getting tired now!" Also, he is hardly doing the workout. He'll do about 30 seconds at a time max before leaving the workout to "teach" good form with one of his students. He is no doubt fit, but it wasn't from doing Insanity. The workouts are a mess. I guess I'm just used to seeing workout videos where everyone is in sync and demonstrating good form. Not here. Poor form everywhere. Everyone is all over the place, and even in some parts of the video there's only like 1/6 people even doing the video. Everyone else is on the floor. I mean, what's the point of making a video that nobody can do??? Isn't Shaun T. the one emphasizing good form the whole time? Yet, the speed at which he's telling the participants (mostly everyone is a fitness instructor) to move is simply impossible. And you don't see him doing it either. Fortunately for me, my dance background allowed me to focus on my own form and not be deterred by what I was seeing on my TV screen.

And for anyone thinking that he's using new and innovative moves, guess again. He just re-named them. Look at any Cathe Friedrich/Jillian Michaels/Jackie Warner video from the past five years and see them doing the same moves as in these videos. They do them timely and in good form.

There are much better DVD workouts out there. In the end, I have to applaud Beachbody for really great marketing. This is an expensive video that I bought into, that many have. And if I want to become a Beachbody "Coach," I can sell their products and receive commision. A+ for marketing!

This workout is definitely hard, and only gets harder. My fear of it only being a workout that made you feel better but not change your body... are slowly slipping away. It was hard though, as I have only gained weight so far, I am far enough in (two weeks) to see fat going away, but I am steady gaining weight, I guess it must be muscle mass underneath my blanket of fat.

I purchased this program set a couple months ago.  I was planning on doing it before the holidays.  I pushed play and got through about 3 days and then the excuses came up and it was back on the shelf.  Well, I let myself go through the holidays and into the New Year.  I got on the scale most recently topping out at 251 pounds at 6'2.  With 40 years old in my near future, I decided to raise the stakes and do this program alongside the TNT Diet. This workout is unlike any that I have ever tried it is cardio at its best. when i first got it i wondered what am i thinking there is no way that i will be able to keep up i thought i was gonna die the first day but you have to remember to dig deep. Insanity is not a gimmic it really does work.

summary: Great workout, but don't expect miracles
text:
I just finished my first round of Insanity last Saturday, and am currently taking a week off before starting my next go around. I'm a female college student, 5'10", 160 lbs or so.

When I was looking at buying Insanity in December I read all kinds of reviews and saw how many people were saying that they lost tons of weight and got in the best shape ever, blah blah blah. I didn't want to lose very much weight, just slim down and get back in shape to start running when it got warm again. So, I bought the program and got started.

The first month was tough at the beginning, but as I kept going it got more and more manageable. By the end I was able to make it all the way through the warm up without having to take a breather, which I figured was pretty good. Then month two came around. I knew it would be harder, but I guess I didn't expect just how physically draining it would be. I have to work out at 6 am because it's the only free time I have during the day, and so it was tough to keep motivated. I also wound up getting really bored with doing the same videos for a whole month, which didn't help the motivation issue.

I did stick with it, though, and completed the program, only missing 2 workouts I think in the whole 63 days. I didn't follow the diet plan because of various reasons, but I still eat pretty healthy. And, I didn't lose any weight. I don't even think I skimmed off any fat in the areas that were bugging me. I pretty much see no change in how I look or how my clothes fit now (though my bf says my butt looks nicer, so I guess I'll believe him on that).

I guess I would recommend Insanity to people who maybe have more weight to lose, or who are able to really devote a lot of time and energy to the videos and diet plan. Like I said, I will be starting another round soon, but this time I altered the schedule to alternate weeks from month 1 and 2, so that I don't get as bored, and I replaced the recovery workouts that I hate with running and yoga days.

In a nutshell it is one of the best workouts I have ever had. I spent a great deal of time researching it on the net before I bought it. If you need a push towards buying this product then I hope this helps, DO IT! I'm technically obese and I know my limits. I did as much of the workout as I could and used the diet program without cheating. In the first 2 weeks I lost almost 3 inches off my waist. It works according to your level of commitment.
Good Luck!

summary: If you put in the effort... you'll get the results.
text: First of all, I am a 22 year old, tall, skinny girl who was sick of having a rail for a frame. I decided on INSANITY since it was the cheaper option overall (and shorter time period) versus P90x. summary: The most challenging and interesting workout

If you want something that pushes you then you should try this!! This is a workout that really is insane! Its good I like how Shaun T. shows you the moves and doesn't expect you just to do them like some other workout dvd's!

summary: Challenging workout but prone to causing injuries
text:
Overall, this is a very good and challenging workout. I completed 7 weeks of the 9 week program and feel that I am in better shape cardiovascularly and my core is stronger. I didn't loose any weight and my body looks no different than when I started. However, I can't recommend this workout to anyone due to its unbalanced approach and high impact movements that can cause injury. I think you can achieve the same results with a lower impact workout. In addition, there is very little stretching (and what there is can be awkward) and Shawn T is not graceful in this respect. Also, there isn't any balance between working chest and back or quads and hamstrings. As a result, my experience suggests that this imbalance can lead to poor posture and potential injury. The lack of stretching is more alarming. I had such cramping in my legs, I couldn't lay flat without pain and had to sleep in the fetal position. It's frustrating because from a fitness perspective, the workouts were enjoyable and effective but just not worth the risk for injury.

I've been working out for over 20 years (I'm 35, 5'9", 155 lbs, male) lifting weights, running, swimming, cycling, hiking, skiing, and practicing yoga. I've never had any serious injury due to any of my exercises. However, I had to stop walking up and down stairs around week 5 of this program even with icing my knees after every workout. I finally decided to stop the workout completely when I could not do the moves during the workout without joint pain (not the "good" burning pain from working out).

Pros:
Challenging
Motivating
Fun Workouts

Cons:
Risk of injury
Imbalanced routine
Awkward stretching and "off" workouts
Unrealistic time commitment (6 days per week and some workouts are 90 minutes)

summary: INSANITY IS HOW MY BODY LOOKS NOW!!! GRAWL!
text: OMG THIS PRODUCT IS ABSOLUTELY AMAIZING I DONT HAVE ANY OTHER WORDS THIS IS BY FAR THE GREATEST THING THAT HAS HAPPENED TO ME (FITNESS WISE) ITS RIDDICULOUS BEEN SEARCHING FOR THIS BODY RESULTS MY WHOLE LIFE!! THANK GOD FOR INSANITY.

I just finished week 7, but I am stopping to mix the program with another one (Rushfit). Since rushfit has no cardio dvd, I'm going to mix the month 2 workouts in on days where cardio is required after I heal for a few days as a means to maintain the gains I've made.

I actually got insanity when it first came out. I was already in decent shape, but decided to check it out as prior to doing it I had finished p90x.

I did both programs to simply get ready to start martial arts again as that's my primary means of staying in shape along with just general physical training (Running, sprints, bodyweight exercises, isometrics, etc...)

I did the first month and I liked it then. I stopped to start Muay Thai (Again) and Brazilian Jiu Jitsu. The first day in Muay Thai I did a lot better than many of the people in my class, but I still gassed faster than I expected, and unfortunately at that time that really discouraged me, so I stopped doing it and decided to move on to my training.

Now I am deployed. I have an even worse work schedule. I've have some of the worst highs and lows through this program. I've had to do two workouts in one day more than once; I've had days where I slept in for 10 hours to recover; I've had days where because of issues I couldn't sleep at all the night before. It was a wild ride. But I pushed through. It's all I really have minus a heavy bag that I occasionally strike, and I have no major qualms with it.

I'm just in it for the cardio and conditioning. It's impeccable the hell you'll put yourself through. I haven't had one day in the second month where I haven't returned with my shirt looking like I took a swim. Yet it's all sweat. If you are ready to take your cardio to a new level: Try this program.

Pros:
- Amazing cardio, core strength and lower body explosive strength built. Ok Upper body strength is built through various movements.
- Simple setup due to no needed equipment (Although a mat is advised). I just pop it in my laptop and I'm game. I've even done a few workouts outside.
- Shaun T is.... Ok in my opinion. He'll ask you to push a lot, but what do you expect? I personally like Tony Horton more personality wise, but Shaun isn't bad.
- I can say that maybe it doesn't apply over completely to certain martial arts training, but I've developed some of the most ridiculous recovery ever, and that does apply over. I guess it's the "Dig deeper" thing? My second wind doesn't always come in, but when it does, it's like I didn't just push myself for the last 20-30 minutes.
I took a fitness test in the middle of the program. I ran a 10 minute 1.5 mile, took a breather for 30 seconds after, and was fine. That hasn't happened to me in I don't know how long.
- The moves occasionally build on one another leading to more complexity, but the after a few workout it become second nature. It's more about blasting than crazier and crazier moves.
- Self-paced progression based results

Cons:
- Your joints are going to take a beating. Do NOT do this program if you have any serious joint issues, especially in your lower body. There are Lots of jumps, squats, and so on. No major issues here minus my shins, but my knee has begun getting "Clicky." I used two mats for most of the program. I still had some days where my shins were screaming at me, and I do stretch them.
- It may not apply over to the sport/activity that you do. It doesn't tout itself as such, but still. Granted after the second month I think what happened to me before would not apply (I could go a couple more rounds than normal).
I take 1/2 a point away because of the first issue though. I'm anticipating the sequel (Insanity: The Asylum) to be a cure for the second con as it is supposed to be more sports based conditioning with higher intensity.

Overall great program.

The product was delivered very quickly and was in good condition.  I am very pleased with the Insanity Fitness workouts!  The workouts are tough and you definitely see results.  These workouts are for any one that is used to working out.

Very much worth the money, the first two weeks are the most difficult to overcome but once that is over, your body is asking for more and more "INSANITY" workout. The results after two weeks are really starting to show, AWESOME program!!!

summary: Insane and Addictive, in a Good Way!
text:
Since I've purchased beachbody.com product before, I knew the workouts would be high-quality: great instruction, clarity, camera work, etc. I am a 48 year old female, 5'4" tall, work full-time, have a long commute (leave house at 6:30am, home at 7pm) and my workouts are limited, for the most part, to weekends. I ran a marathon over 10 years ago, but it's been a slow decline since (I'm about 15 pounds overweight). I chose this over P90x because I travel a lot for work and thought I could just take the DVDs with me on the road and pop them into a DVD in a hotel room (I have, works out great). Most of the workouts in phase 1 are around 40 minutes so I figured I'd be able to fit this into my schedule (phase 2 is upwards of 45 to around an hour). Let me tell you, this is one tough workout--you will break a sweat and be winded during the warm up phase, i.e., in the first 5 minutes or so. Basically, these tapes are a lot of football and track drills, squats, push-ups, plyometrics and you do each segment 3 times--for example, you have a warm up segment, and do the first set slow, second set medium, and third as fast as you can. Take a short break and then next segment. The breaks are short and the sets are long (i.e., max interval training), yet they are easy to follow. The routines are very-well structured--i.e., you work alternatve muscle groups (quads, then your hamstrings, etc.) then when you're about to keel over, there's an "active" break where you slowly bring your heartrate down. Like all beachbody products, there's a timer that you can watch in the lower part of the screen so you can count the seconds until your next break. Even the "cast members" in the DVDs have to take breaks and drop out to recover for a few seconds...and Shaun T does from time-to-time as well. The cast members can't speak at times while they're doing the workout, and I will say that I work so hard at times I can't speak either. These routines are tough, but I will say this: if I had the time (and stamina) every day to do these routines, I would because they are so energizing. They are really hard, but fun and addictive.

While the routines are hard, what really makes this DVD is Shaun T., the instructor. He gives clear, concise directions, gives great advice throughout on form that makes a real difference in its effect (some of which I've never heard before), is enthusiastic, fun and funny, motivating and seems sincere. It seems like he is totally into these works. Plus, he is one incredible physical specimen. This guy is in awesome physical shape and it is amazing to see what he does in these DVDs--it's like watching a thoroughbred. The guy has fabulous footwork and coordination, is fast, strong, doesn't give up, stays high energy throughout, gives great tips on form, counts for you, acknowledges how hard it is, does the routines WITH you (instead of instructing most of the time) and basically has pogo sticks for legs(I can't believe how high he can jump.) Plus, as odd as it may seem, he seems so sincere when he is rooting for you to "Dig Deeper" and "You can do it" that it almost seems like he is talking to you directly.

The first few times you do each routine (i.e., cardio, circuit, plyo) are really the hardest in terms of exertion and getting used to it. I can't fit 6x a week into my schedule, so I do this 4x a week and have really seen the results. I am being careful about what I eat but am not following the diet. If you do this 6x a week, as instructed, the fat will melt off. And if you follow the diet, you will drop major weight. And you will find that your stamina increases by leaps and bounds. I had been doing Insanity for a month, and was on vacation and went for a run. I hadn't run in 2 or 3 months. I went out for a 4 mile run in a hilly area and I have never run hills with such ease. It was like running on flat ground. You will find Insanity to be highly motivating.

I do wish there were some alternate moves provided. But I guess they want you to "aim high" and try things outside your comfort zone. But you will need to go at your own pace, and modify accordingly. I did find my calves to be tight, so you may have to do a bit of supplemental stretching on your own if your muscles get really tight.

TOUGH, BUT HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

The package arrived quickly in 3 days.  Every DVD so far has been perfect, no complaints!  I just realized that I have the "DELUXE" package which includes 2 extra discs.  Only thing is, I do not have a CARDIO CIRCUIT DVD, but I think there is a misprint in that they mean the PLYOMETRIC CARDIO CIRCUIT for the scheduled day.  Workouts are very challenging and I look forward to popping in that dvd every morning!!!

I read many reviews before I purchased this product because I wasn't sure if I could do it.  I am female, 47, and consider myself in good shape.....for my age.  I've had some injuries (biggest problem is achilles) and I wasn't sure I could keep up with the program.  I am on my 8th day and I find it to be very motivating. I do the DVD at my pace, which is getting better every workout as I learn the routine and my body adjusts to the exercises.  However, I would say that if you have major joint issues this is not for you.  My husband has had knee and ankle surgery and he would not attempt this for fear of re-injury.  I actually do some brisk walking and other stretching before I even start the DVD because I can't go right into jogging and jumping (no matter how low intensity to start) without being warmed up.
Very, very pleased.  The product was exactly as advertised.  Mike made that extra effort and shipped by Priority Mail at no additional cost.  Great!

summary: BE READY TO DIG DEEP...AND LOVE IT!!!
text:
I'll keep this very simple. I was nervous about acquiring Insanity, especially after seeing all sorts of recommendations that one should be in reasonable shape prior to getting into Insanity. While there is a little truth to that, I don't know if that is as much of a concern as joint pains would be. I'm not in the best shape, but I have done well with this routine. I am now on my seventh week, and I already considered this to be my greatest investment before I was even done with the first month.

I started off at 210 lbs. I am now down to 196 lbs and managed to also shave over 12 inches off my body in the process. I am not going to get into any more detail, but I will say this. Insanity is very appropriately named. For those of you who want a physical challenge, this is it! For those of you who think you are supposed to get used to Insanity, think again. The reality is - no matter how much you get used to it, or how much your endurance builds - you are always expected to go all out all the time. The object is to do better, not to keep up!

If you are still in a contemplating process, that's fine, I understand because I was the same way. I got it now, and it has made all the difference!
This workout is insane!  I have worked out in the gym for hours at a time and never sweat like this before.  It is a very hard workout but worth every penny.

Love it! About to start Month 2 and I can't believe the change in my body. I was in good shape when I started, but definitely didn't have the plyometrics/leg strength base that this workout requires, so I've been playing catch-up. If you think you might not be in good enough condition to try this program, go ahead and get it and let month 1 serve as a foundation. If you follow the Elite Nutrition guide and keep "pushing play" you are guaranteed to see results. My only regret is I wish I'd ordered the deluxe package, because I've heard so many great things about the two DVDs included in that.

I have weak wrists and an old injury in my left ankle, but as of Day 36, the program hasn't caused me any pain. I do the workouts in Vibram "barefoot" shoes because I found it to be more stable than even my best cross trainers.

This workout program is not good. Basically, one does the same workout again and again and again, with just slight variations of the moves that do not make any substantial difference. The 'theory' of this program, which it proudly tells you, is that it makes Interval training harder, by taking out the interval rest period, so that it is no longer an interval (?). The plyometrics do not follow any of the protocols of plyo training that you can find on any university physical education Web site.
The form of the background exercises is also poor. There is one, a young blonde woman, who always does her squats etc. with her spine hunched over in a "C"-shape that makes my back hurt just watching her. She is never corrected in her form.
The company, Beachbody, that puts this out also has a multi-level marketing program, so that there is no shortage of people who will sell this to you on the Web and offer to become your 'coach', the only qualification to be a coach seems to be a willingness to sign up other 'coaches' from what I can see.
The same company also puts out the much advertised P90X which actually is a very good general conditioning program. It actually alternates days of weight training days vs. cardio/yoga days so that one doesn't overwork one area too much. There is weight work, yoga, stretching, kickboxing moves, plyometrics, something for everyone. For a lot of people this is all they will need to meet the advice of 'take exercise'. If one wanted more of a cardio-based routine, I would probably go with 'RushFit' which is co-hosted with George St. Pierre.
As for Insanity, you'd have to be nuts to make this the centre of your program.

I am the classic Beachbody target - just turned 40, had 30 pounds to lose, felt like crap. As a former long distance runner, I knew what it was like to be in great shape, but man had I let myself slip.

So I set myself a goal - lose 30 pounds, and 7 inches off my waist.

There was only one complication - I made a bet with 2 other buddies to see who could lose the largest percentage of body weight in 12 weeks. This meant that I needed to find something that would get me into rip roaring, navel winking shape in extremely short order.

This, of course led me to Insanity, which claimed to turn pretzel pounding lardasses like myself into striated demigods in 63 agonizing days. Perfect. Sign me up. The only catch was that it said you already had to be in some semblance of physical shape to undertake the heavy workouts they would deliver. So, I quit smoking and decided that was as good a start as I was going to get, and kicked things off the next day.

Ooooh, daddy....

The first week passed by in a bit of a blur, but to my credit I did not yarp like many of the other folks here seem to have done. I did, however fight to hold body and soul together. Just the opening warmup was a killer, and that (without belaboring the obvious) was just the warmup.

The workouts are very good, and Shawn T keeps you motivated throughout. Things do get repetitive, however, and a couple of the steel bellied assistants they have in the background get brutally annoying. Tanya(sp?) manages to keep a Topol smile plastered on her face throughout, and by minute 32 I (and I'm sure many others) want to shoot her out of a cannon into a parallel galaxy where she can smile and clap excitedly while doing endless leg lifts somewhere far, far away.

As a person who was fat enough to be dodging my own tits through the first workouts, I would say that it is possible to start the Insanity program without a huge amount of physical conditioning. That said, if that is the route you are going to take, get ready to suffer real good for about 2 weeks as your body gets acclimated. I would also guess that the chance of injury is increased quite a bit if you start out unfit, but I was lucky there and did not have much issue in that regard.

I did not stick to the diet religiously, but have kept very low carb since I began the workouts. The weight loss is pretty amazing - I am now in the first week of month 2, and am 10 pounds down. With the super intense second month just starting, I would guess that I will easily lose another 10 pounds before the 2nd month finishes. That will mean I will be 20 pounds done with my 30 pound weight loss goal, in only 2 months.

A quick note on the 2nd month - it really is tough. Just when you have gotten used to the first month's workout, they switch it up on you. The workouts are about 15 minutes longer, and every minute of that extra time is spent driving you until you drop. I am just getting used to the pace, and actually it is very doable, but there is no way you can finish without being totally exhausted, with your clothes absolutely soaked with sweat. Also, as many people have said, there is no way to do every rep of every exercise. Just do the best you can, and don't sweat the rest.

All in all, this product works exactly as advertised - great results, but you will have to work your a$$ of to get them.

I first want to say that I am an overweight, 24 year old female and this video is truly insane. I have been doing this video for a short time, but I can say that it feels great. I have purchased a number of videos trying to get the weight off that came on from stress, eating, and more stress, and Insanity is the only one that makes me want to keep going and provides results.

Shaun T makes working out hard, but rewarding. I was apprehensive about beginning this workout because many people were saying you needed to be fit and in shape to do it...WORNG! I do agree that you need to be somewhat active to get going. This Fit Test will have you drenching in sweat. With each workout, you will find yourself doing better and better. I had to modify many things at first, but I now see that I can make my jumps higher and endure longer.

A bonus for me is when I think it's too hard, I look at Shaun T's team and see them taking a break, and know that if they can take a break and they are fit, I can. And sometimes they are breaking and I am still going, and that makes me feel great.

Ladies, I love my hair done, my nails painted and manicured, wearing pink, and skirts and sandals.. so I am as girly as they come. If I can do this, so can you. Worry about your hair the hour after you've finished. I keep going and know that my hair is not as important as my health. Don't be afraid.

After trying many things, I found this DVD to make you want to keep going. I find me telling myself that it is only 60 days. On mornings I don't want to get up, I think, come on it's just 45 minutes and the rest of your life. Results are bound to come if you committ.

This workout is amazing. No matter how many times you've been through the videos, you will sweat. Its a bit hard on the knees, ankles and wrists, so steer clear if these are sensitive spots for you. I love doing it, the time commitment each day isn't too huge, but the payoff is awesome. I'm three weeks in and have already see results, the muscle definition that is starting to happen is very exciting. In two weeks I start the 1 hour sessions which will be even more insane.

Just started this program a few weeks ago and have started to see some improvement, not much weight loss yet though, but I have not followed the meal plan 100%.  I am anxious to get through the 60 days!
I bought this for the teenage child of a friend. She is using it to lose weight and work on her abs.

This is absolutely the hardest workout i have ever tried, if you are a begginer please don't buy this program, even the warmups leaved me sweating.

I would recommend this product to people that have a good cardio but wan to make it better, if yo aren't athletic please don't try this workout it's VERY HARD

Follow the directions, and you get in amazing shape for working out less than 39 minutes a day. Couldn't be happier. Way less painful/boring than the treadmill, way more effective & healthy.

If you're more into looking good/bulking up, I'd go with P90X.

This is by far the BEST exercise plan I have ever can't across. The only problem is that I can't use it! If you live in a apartment building with annoying neighbors this is not for you. So much jumping, running and heavy foot moves that I can't use it cause my super knocks on my door every time. For this price, this thing should have came with a 5 inch thick exercise mat that will muffled the noise so my neighbors won't complain. Other than that, I only got to use it for three days and I could tell it was the real deal. The diet plan is pretty expensive to keep up with though.

I used to run a few times a week and go to the gym, but I never really had the abs or tone that I wanted. I tried this DVD and within a week I could see results. Now I'm almost at 4 weeks and I love it. I can actually say I'm addicted to it. It has made me look completely different and Shaun T is an excellent motivator. DEFINITELY worth the money!!

This is by far my favorite workout routine/system. I have never encountered anything like it before. The basic moves look very simple and the type of thing you could do without much exertion, but that is a misconception. For those who claim the system does not work, I would question their diet and how intense they worked out. The workout is intense, but ultimately you control the how hard you push through the intensity.

Admittedly, there are two downsides to this workout. First, there is a bunch of jumping so doing it in an apartment is tough. Second, due to the intensity and moves, you may have some joint discomfort. Personally, I have been able to work around both of these issues. Regarding the apartment issue I have gone as far as to workout outside, or to move around some of the equipment at my apartment gym to make room (you don't need much but if you apartment is anything like mine, they cram a lot into a small space). I have had some joint discomfort and have found it eased by two things: first, the better my diet the less likely I am to have any discomfort; and second, when I hurt I am always able to identify a move that I am doing incorrectly.

I know many people that have done P90X, including myself, and those who I have convinced to give Insanity a shot all agree that it is much more intense. It is just intense in a different way.

summary: Results don't lie--AS LONG AS YOUR UP FOR THE CHALLENGE!
text:
Before my review, I must state what by now should be obvious to you: THIS IS NOT FOR BEGINNERS! If you are not already in good shape, click away, select a different program, and come back in a few months. Also, if you have knee or joint issues, this may not be for you--actually, it's not for you.

Ok. Now that you are warned, a discussion on my results:

I completed the program and followed the nutrition guide to the letter (remember: 80% nutrition, 20% exercise!). After the 63-day ordeal, I have dropped 2 pants sizes (I'm a size 30 for the first time since 8th grade), lost 17 pounds of pure fat, completely overhauled my cardio endurance, toned my muscles, learned how to eat right, and built a six-pack. When I started, I had no aspirations of building a rock-solid core. I thought genetics were fighting me and that getting a six-pack was a naive dream. However, here I am and I can't believe the mirror when I see my core. My girlfriend's reaction was amazing (we are long-distance and she hadn't seen me since I completed the first month), her only words were "wow, I can't wait to wash my clothing on your abs." I still have that little stubborn pocket of belly fat, but I am very confident that a second round through will rip me even more. (for my second round, I am doing INSANITY every other day and mixing in the weight exercises from P90X to build muscle--this way I remain lean and fit and can gain muscle mass).

The first month is essentially a conditioning month to help you gain endurance for the second month. Make sure you have adequate footwear and enough space to do the workout. I also recommend a plyo-mat (though good ones are a bit expensive), heart rate monitor, and taking joint support supplements.

I am a third-year law student at an ivy league school--if I was able to squeeze one hour a day for INSANITY you can too!

People who have given INSANITY bad reviews generally do so because they got pirated discs that didn't work or are not in good enough shape to get through the program.

summary: If you need to take your fitness to a new level, this really works
text:
As a former fat guy who never wants to return to that state and a current health and gym nut, I'm a veteran of various workout programs. I've tried several home workout DVD's in my life and without exception hated them all. Insanity changed all that and honestly changed my life.

I was already in great shape when I started Insanity. I could run ten miles with ease, held my own in strength, and spent 90 minutes in the gym six days a week. I picked Insanity because I wanted to take my fitness to a whole new level and get the perfect definition and tone that had always eluded me. I expected very little. I was insanely wrong.

When I first started doing Insanity, it kicked my butt, then for good measure kicked it some more. Insanity is interval training, which means doing short intervals of intense activity followed by a short break. It's very tough. These aren't the wimpy exercises you learned in gym class. They are intense resistance moves that have even the fitness models (and occasionally Shaun T, the developer and host) on the ground and sucking air.

After the first couple of days, I could barely walk I was so sore, let alone squat down. However, I pushed through and the soreness went away. Each day of Insanity remained tough because the workouts exhaust the muscles, but they were always do-able. Regardless, you can always take a rest break and then get back to working out.

Best of all, I began to see incredible results very quickly. I could see definition in new areas, including those elusive abs after a week. After two weeks, my wife saw me with my shirt off and told me it was the best she'd ever seen my body. And, keep in mind, I'd spent tons of time in the gym previously. My body is truly the most toned and fit it's ever been. For the first time in my life, I'm really ready for the beach.

I must add, however, that I don't follow the Insanity "plan." My wife does and has also seen great results. I do Insanity and supplement it with running, hiking, sports, the gym, and sometimes, even more Insanity. My transformation has been so amazing that, yes, I sometimes rewind and re-do parts of the DVDs. I don't follow the nutrition plan either, but it looks solid. I just eat healthily and always get enough protein, especially after working out.

I want to say it again: this program is tough; kick your butt, suck air on the floor type tough. I had to clean the rug near my TV because it has so much of my sweat and my wife's. If you're a beginner, this program isn't for you. The warning to consult your doctor isn't just a formality here. Insanity is geared for people of an intermediate to advanced fitness level.

Finally, Insanity will work if you do it. It's hard as all get out and many will quit. But, if you stick it out, you'll see results. It would be impossible not to. I started out a huge skeptic, but am now an Insanity devotee. Now I can't wait to finish it up and move on to Asylum. Oh, and to hit the beach this summer.

summary: Game Changer but not a Life Chnger
text:
Like some other reviewers I had done P90x and wanted something to keep me in shape while I took a break from it. This is an awesome program that works you to the point of exhaustion every time. After a couple weeks your aerobic base is through the roof you feel like your heart rate can stay in the zone for longer and longer. And your recovery time is shorter.

But despite all its benefits I think it is only good for an interim workout to whip you into shape rather than something you can continue to use over and over again. It's very intense and it doesn't let up and I just wonder if anyone could keep that kind of routine up over an extended period of time.

By comparison, P90x is more of a long term life changer. It is methodical and evenly paced. You work muscles which burn fat and you work at a pace that keeps your heart rate and breathing up. With Insanity you're constantly sucking air like you've just sprinted a mile. It's as much mental as physical because you have to constantly make yourself keep going. The difference between the two programs is like the parable of the father and son bull looking over the herd of cows in the valley below them. The son says to the father "Hey dad, let's run down there and f*** one of those cows!" And the dad says "No son, let's walk down...and f*** 'em all."

That being said, Insanity has improved me in many ways that makes P90x better. It helped my balance, stretching, endurance (of course) and my "attack" (if that makes sense). For example in P90x warm ups I know to lift my knees better and why it's important to do that.

So my recommendation is to buy this program but don't think of it as the end all be all of workouts. It is an excellent compliment to P90x or any other weight training program. And you will learn a lot about warming up, stretching, balance, endurance and yourself.

summary: Great, but don't expect to look like him
text:
Right. I have this workout, I have done it for nearly all 2 months now, and am very happy with it. The following are merely concerns that should be considered by others contemplating this as a means of fitness.

First, if you have weak knees, try something else. This program involves a LOT of jumping.

Second, if you wish or require a steady (no stops) program, this might not be what you are looking for. That could definitely have been one of the features here. As is, Shaun T. stops between exercises to show the viewers how to do the following one. That makes sense, right? Sure, the first time you see it. When you have already been doing the program for weeks, however, you know how to do them. All he would need to do was say "Okay, Ski Abs [one of the exercises], everybody. Go!" If you had briefly forgotten what "Ski Abs" was, you could look at the screen and see him and the whole group doing them. You could keep going, and that would take the intensity level to another level. It could be an option for "version II" of this. As is, to maintain the intensity level while doing this program I am running in place waiting for him to get going again while he is explaining an exercise I already know perfectly well.

Third, and most importantly, this program is not likely to get you to look like the gentleman on the cover. There are folks out there with that incredible genetic code (e.g., Herschel Walker, former pro football player, built like a statue and won the Heisman Trophy in college by doing no upper body training except pushups), but not many. This program will shape you, definitely, but it will not get you to look like the exercise coordinator or his participants onscreen, all of whom look like bathing suit models. To get that - to get ripped - you are going to have to lift weights too. The abdominal workout here is not that intense, it just isn't. Unless you have that gift-from-God genetic code you will get no six-pack from doing it. You will need to do the other exercises body-sculpted people do, and LOTS more of them than displayed here (20 minutes?? Forget it!).

All in all, however, this is a great product. I have survived it, I have enjoyed it, and will keep doing it. If you are thinking about getting it, GET it! And Dig Deeper...

First, Insanity is not the "most extreme" or "most difficult" program out there. The program reminded me of my experience in JROTC Raiders in High School. This does not mean the program is worthless, or even average. It is very good, and will certainly improve your fitness, no matter what level you're at. The line "Shaun T's brand-new program is the most extreme, most difficult, and most rewarding workout you will EVER try" is just for selling points. Second, consult a doctor before you try this program. It is not for people with fairly weak joints. I'm in excellent shape, but I have to stop regularly to give my ankle or shin a break. Having the right shoes isn't a way to get out of this problem. The shoes I have are almost brand new, and were fitted based on the unique way I walk. In short, if you're not physically able to endure this program, without joint or back pain, then find something else. Third, Shaun T isn't there to coach YOU personally. He cannot see you or adjust his workouts to your personal needs. If you fall down, throw up, or something blows out, the recording will simply say something like, "Let's go, Let's go!" or "Alright, let's pick it up." In short if you want to have an extreme workout experience, and lose weight, gain weight, or improve in fitness in a short amount of time, get a personal trainer who you can trust. It may be more expensive, but it will help with YOUR needs much better than any recorded program ever could. Thank you for reading this, and good luck with your training.
